- In person, in London. We value synchronous communication.

- Debate rigorously, decide quickly, execute relentlessly.

- Enjoy the journey. Hard problems, good colleagues.

The role

We’re building the AI platform freight forwarders rely on. We started with quoting and are expanding across the shipment lifecycle. As Product Lead, you will be central to that expansion, helping decide where we focus and turning those decisions into products customers depend on.

What you’ll do: 

- Own product outcomes: Own the roadmap, priorities and performance of specific products, from defining the customer problem through launch, rollout and adoption. Partner with the founders on overall product direction and strategy.

- Build from customer insight: Work closely with freight forwarders across commercial and operational roles. Understand how they work, identify the problems customers share and build products for those needs rather than one-off solutions.

- Prototype and build: Turn ideas into working prototypes and early product versions, using AI tools and code to test them with customers. Work hands-on with engineering to take promising ideas into production, not just write specs and hand them over.

- Drive product expansion: Build a clear view of the market, including where we win, where we do not compete and why customers choose us. Use that understanding to identify the next workflows Nexcade should enter and turn them into products that grow revenue.

- Raise the standard of product thinking: Define success measures, test assumptions and examine accuracy, edge cases and second-order effects before scaling. Write clear specs and decision documents, including a written recommendation on the hard calls.

- Build the product operating system: Establish a clear planning and decision-making cadence without adding bureaucracy. Make sure product meetings are well prepared, teams have the context they need and decisions translate into shipped work.

- Make product and platform trade-offs: Work closely with engineering to decide when to invest in shared capabilities and when a faster, product-specific approach is right.

What we look for 

- Strong product judgement: You have owned meaningful product work in a complex B2B product and can show how your decisions changed customer behaviour or business results. You define success clearly and test assumptions, accuracy and edge cases before scaling.

- Product taste: You can turn complex workflows into products that feel simple, coherent and trustworthy. You care about the details that make people choose to use them.

- Technical fluency: You work effectively with strong engineers, understand trade-offs across architecture, AI, data and integrations and bring the customer and product perspective to choices about speed, quality and reuse.

- Excellent judgement: You get beyond what customers ask for to understand how their work really happens and distinguish repeatable needs from bespoke requests. You use customer and market insight to make product choices that drive adoption, expansion and revenue.

- High agency and directness: You take ownership, hold a high bar and disagree openly and constructively. You are comfortable with ambiguity, fast iteration and changing priorities.

- Obsess over the problem: You are drawn to complex, messy problems in industries the economy depends on and want to understand how the people and systems behind them really work. Industry experience is a bonus, but not required.

Why join 

The biggest product choices are still ahead: how deep we go, where we expand and how everything fits together. Our product is already live with leading freight forwarders and this role will shape what comes next. You will build AI for the work that keeps global trade moving, alongside a team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will get meaningful equity in the company you help build.

title: Software Engineer
description:
About us

People assume the supply chain is an automated, algorithmic system. It is not. It is a large number of people acting as the glue between organisations and systems, doing work the world depends on with tools that have barely changed in decades. Nexcade builds AI agents for those people, starting in freight forwarding, a $210BN industry.

Our agents are live in production with some of the leading global forwarders, pricing millions in freight every week, and we are expanding the platform deeper into the shipment lifecycle. We have raised $8.5M to make this a reality.

Our founders, Dan and Tasho, spent years at Sedna and Palantir working with supply chain companies on problems like this one. We are backed by top VCs and angels who backed or founded Synthesia, n8n and other world-class companies.

How we work

- Everybody codes, founders included. The whole company is technical, commercial team included, and runs on coding agents.

- Closely with customers and design partners, so what we ship changes how they operate.

- At pace. Fast cycles and quick iterations, on the product and on how we work.

- End to end. If you see something broken or missing, you have the freedom (and the responsibility) to fix it.

- In person, 4+ days a week in London. We value synchronous communication.

- Debate rigorously, decide quickly, execute relentlessly.

- Enjoy the journey. Hard problems, good colleagues.

The role

We are building the AI platform for freight forwarding and expanding our product surface, and we are hiring software engineers across product, AI and platform to do it.

You will build products that do freight forwarding work alongside our customers' teams, operating across the entire shipment lifecycle. You will work across the stack in Python, TypeScript and React, and directly with customers and founders on what gets built.

Everyone here works across the stack, but each engineer has a spike: the area where they set the bar for the team. You spend most of your time where yours is, and lean on your colleagues where theirs are.

- Product: You build best in class products for the core jobs in freight forwarding, one job at a time. You work as a design partner with our customers to understand the work deeply, turn that understanding into a product they would choose over anything else, and feed what you learn back into the platform everyone builds on.

- AI: You raise the ceiling on what our AI can do and the floor on how reliably it does it. That spans high volume tasks like classification and extraction and deep workflow tasks that run for hours. You design for performance, reliability, explainability and control, set up the gyms and evals to measure them, and build the harness that runs our agents in all of our products.

- Platform: You own the foundation every product stands on: the runtime for thousands of concurrent agents and workflows, the way they communicate and scale, the controls for how they access data with permissions that hold, and the observability to see and measure all of it. You ensure the rest of the team can move fast without fear.

What we look for

- A spike, with evidence. Something you have been exceptional at and proof of it. We hire on slope rather than years, so there is no experience threshold in either direction.

- Strong fundamentals. In the AI-assisted era, having good technical judgement is key. You have shipped production systems people depend on, seen them fail and learned from it.

- High agency and ownership. You take an ambiguous problem, make a call, and see it through.

- Humility and learning velocity. You want to get better and you change your mind when the evidence says so.

- Interest in the problem. You do not need a freight background, but you need to find messy real-world operations interesting rather than a chore.

Why join

You will shape the product, the architecture and the company, working alongside an engineering team from Palantir, Raft, Faculty, UnlikelyAI and Oxford. You will work directly with the businesses using what you build, on AI applied to an industry that has resisted software for decades. You will get meaningful equity, so when this works you share in it.

title: Assistant Financial Controller
description:
About Flock

Road accidents kill and injure people, damage vehicles, and cost businesses fortunes. But traditional insurance does nothing to prevent them - it just pays out claims when they happen. At Flock, we’re changing that. Using telematics, AI, and real-time data, we proactively help our fleet customers prevent crashes. We obsessively focus on keeping drivers safe, and we put our money where our mouth is - paying out millions of pounds per year to fleets that get safer over time.

We were acquired by Admiral in May 2026. Now we combine the backing of the UK’s leading motor insurer with startup energy and speed. We’re growing fast with bigger plans than ever, and we’re hugely optimistic that our approach will save many more lives in the decade ahead.

We’re on a mission to make the world quantifiably safer. Join us!

About the role

Reporting to Sarah Phillips, you’ll own month-end for Flock’s finance team and strengthen the controls around it, running the close and producing the variance analysis and MI that FP&A and our senior team use for budgeting and reporting. We’re automating finance on our new platform and the team uses AI every day, so there’s plenty of room to improve how the work gets done as well as doing it.

It suits a recently qualified accountant with strong core accounting from practice, who has already improved a process or control somewhere and wants to keep growing within the finance team.

What you’ll be doing

- Own the month-end close from start to finish so it lands accurately and on time.

- Prepare balance sheet reconciliations and post journals, keeping the ledger clean and well evidenced.

- Run variance analysis and build the monthly MI pack, explaining what moved and why.

- Strengthen our financial controls and automate manual steps wherever you find them.

- Prepare our VAT returns and assist with group reporting.

- Work with FP&A so the numbers behind budgets and senior reporting are right.

- Support the annual audit and work alongside our external auditors.

- Use AI tools in your daily work to speed up reconciliations, analysis and reporting, and share what works with the team.

- Pick up ad hoc finance projects, including R&D tax claims if you have the experience.

What you’ll need

- An ACA qualification, ideally recently qualified, although we’ll also consider strong ACCA or CIMA candidates.

- A practice background with hands-on month-end experience, whether from non-audit client work or time in industry. Big 4 or not makes no difference to us.

- Solid core accounting and close attention to detail, including balance sheet reconciliations, journals and variance analysis.

- Experience strengthening financial controls or improving a finance process, with an example you can talk us through.

- Curiosity and ambition, with the drive to push things forward and keep learning.

- An interest in AI. You don’t need to be an expert, but you should already be using it at work or in your own time and want to do more with it.

Nice to have:

- Audit experience.

- Experience using NetSuite.

- Experience automating finance processes.

- Exposure to R&D tax claims.

- Experience in the tech sector.

Benefits

- 25 days of holiday (+ Bank Holidays) 🏖

- Share Incentive Plan 📈

- Workplace Pension 💰

- Private Medical Insurance 🏥 (including Dental 🦷 Optical 👓 & Mental Health 💆‍♀️ support options)

- Various Salary Sacrifice Schemes - Holiday Purchase, Tech, Gym, Cycle to Work, Electric Vehicle, Private Medical Insurance for families 💵

- Enhanced Parental Leave and Pay 🐣

- £1000 toward relevant professional qualifications 🎓

- £500 per annum towards learning and development 🌱

- 3 days paid leave for L&D purposes 🌻

We work hybrid, typically three days a week in our Central London office (fewer office days can be accommodated for longer commute times), a few minutes from Moorgate and Liverpool Street. Visits to client sites, conferences and broker offices count towards office days.

Making the world quantifiably safer takes more than good data. It takes a team where different perspectives are heard, and that’s a priority here. We insure fleets and drivers from every background, and we know a team built the same way makes sharper decisions and a better product for our customers. So we hire on merit, full stop, and we actively encourage applications from everyone. If you don’t tick every box, apply anyway. Just come as your genuine self: the qualities and experiences only you bring are exactly what we want.

title: Sr. Software Engineer, Cloud Platform
description:
Who we are 

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale. 

Working at Samsara means you'll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that's shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you'll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term. 

About the role: 

As a Senior Engineer in the Infrastructure org, you will help evolve the cloud foundations behind every Samsara product. Your goal will be to reduce systemic production risk and enable continued growth by making infrastructure safer to change, easier to operate, and more resilient and cost-efficient at scale.

You will bring deep expertise in at least one infrastructure domain, such as compute and workload orchestration, networking, storage and stateful systems, or cloud control planes, and apply it across our multi-account, multi-region AWS environment. You will lead work such as modernizing compute and stateful infrastructure, strengthening capacity and failure isolation, and building standardized infrastructure-as-code workflows and reusable automation.

You will partner with product engineering teams to turn recurring risks and manual operations into durable platforms and paved paths. We do not expect you to be an expert in every infrastructure domain. We are looking for engineers who have built and operated critical systems at significant scale, understand how infrastructure fails, and can use that experience to improve both our platforms and our engineering practices.

You should apply if: 

- You want to impact the industries that run our world: The software, firmware, and hardware you build will result in real-world impact, helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.

- You are a life-long learner: We have ambitious goals. Every Samsarian has a growth mindset as we work with a wide range of technologies, challenges, and customers that push us to learn on the go.

- You believe customers are more than a number: Samsara engineers enjoy a rare closeness to the end user and you will have the opportunity to participate in customer interviews, collaborate with customer success and product managers, and use metrics to ensure our work is translating into better customer outcomes.

- You are a team player: Working on our Samsara Engineering teams requires a mix of independent effort and collaboration. Motivated by our mission, we're all racing toward our connected operations vision, and we intend to win together.

In this role, you will: 

- Design, build, and operate reliable cloud platforms, bringing depth in one or more areas such as compute, networking, storage, stateful systems, or infrastructure control planes.

- Improve the scalability, capacity management, isolation, recovery, and cost efficiency of critical production infrastructure.

- Build standardized infrastructure-as-code workflows and reusable automation that support self-service provisioning, testing, progressive rollout, reconciliation, rollback, and drift prevention. 

- Identify shared failure modes and build safeguards that prevent localized failures from escalating into broad customer impact.

- Contribute to multi-account, multi-region, and isolated AWS architectures, including regulated environments such as GovCloud.

- Participate in operational ownership and incident response, using incidents and near misses to drive durable architectural improvements.

- Mentor engineers, raise the quality of infrastructure design and operational judgment, and establish patterns that can be adopted across the organization.

- Clearly communicate architecture, trade-offs, risks, and migration plans to technical and organizational stakeholders.

- Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices.

Minimum requirements for this role. 

- 6+ years of experience designing and building software, infrastructure, or distributed systems, including operating critical systems in production.

- Deep expertise in at least one of the following: compute and workload orchestration, networking, storage and stateful systems, or cloud infrastructure control planes.

- Strong software-engineering fundamentals in Go, Python, Java, or a similar language.

- Hands-on experience designing and operating infrastructure on a major public cloud platform; AWS experience is preferred.

- Experience using infrastructure as code, such as Terraform, to safely manage production infrastructure.

- Strong understanding of capacity management, failure domains, observability, rollout safety, and production recovery.

- Demonstrated ability to lead complex technical initiatives across teams and through ambiguous problem spaces.

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or equivalent practical experience

An ideal candidate also has: 

- Designing and operating large-scale compute or container platforms such as ECS, EKS, Kubernetes, or similar orchestration systems.

- Designing and operating stateful distributed systems such as Kafka, OpenSearch, managed databases, caching, or large-scale storage platforms.

- Building internal infrastructure platforms, control planes, or self-service developer experiences adopted across multiple teams.

- Designing multi-account or multi-region cloud architectures with strong workload isolation and disaster recovery.

- Leading major infrastructure migrations while maintaining availability and controlling operational risk.

- Delivering measurable improvements in infrastructure capacity, cost efficiency, or developer self-service.

Total Rewards 

At Samsara, we build for the people who keep the global economy moving. We want owners, not passengers, which is why our rewards are designed to fuel high-impact builders. Our compensation program delivers above-market total compensation through a combination of base salary, performance-based bonus/variable pay, and equity (for eligible roles) in a high-growth public company. We meaningfully differentiate pay for our top performers, who have the opportunity to earn above-market compensation that can outpace the broader market over time.

Beyond compensation, we provide the foundations that enable long-term success: a flexible, employee-led remote model, a professional development stipend, comprehensive health and parental leave plans, and more. If you're ready to build for the long term and own the outcome, your journey starts here.

Flexible Working 

At Samsara, we embrace a flexible working model that caters to the diverse needs of our teams. Our offices are open for those who prefer to work in-person and we also support remote work where it aligns with our operational requirements. For certain positions, being close to one of our offices or within a specific geographic area is important to facilitate collaboration, access to resources, or alignment with our service regions. In these cases, the job description will clearly indicate any working location requirements. Our goal is to ensure that all members of our team can contribute effectively, whether they are working on-site, in a hybrid model, or fully remotely. All offers of employment are contingent upon an individual's ability to secure and maintain the legal right to work at the company and in the specified work location, if applicable. 

Belonging at Samsara 

At Samsara, we welcome everyone regardless of their background. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, national origin, sex, gender, gender identity, sexual orientation, protected veteran status, disability, age, and other characteristics protected by law. We depend on the unique approaches of our team members to help us solve complex problems and want to ensure that Samsara is a place where people from all backgrounds can make an impact.

Accommodations 

Samsara is an inclusive work environment, and we are committed to ensuring equal opportunity in employment for qualified persons with disabilities. Please email click here if you require any reasonable accommodations throughout the recruiting process.

Our Commitment to Authenticity 

We use Tofu , a fraud detection tool, to validate the authenticity of applications and protect against identity fraud. This ensures we are connecting with real people and allows us to prioritize genuine candidates. Please see Samsara's Candidate Privacy Notice for more information.

description:

Backed by a recent Series C led by leading global investors and strategic partners, Deepgram has processed over 50,000 years of audio and transcribed more than 1 trillion words. There is no organization in the world that understands voice better than Deepgram.

Company Operating Rhythm 

At Deepgram, we expect an AI-first mindset—AI use and comfort aren’t optional, they’re core to how we operate, innovate, and measure performance.

Every team member who works at Deepgram is expected to actively use and experiment with advanced AI tools, and even build your own into your everyday work. Additionally, we move at the pace of AI. Change is rapid, and you can expect your day-to-day work to evolve just as quickly. This may not be the right role if you’re not excited to experiment, adapt, think on your feet, and learn constantly, or if you’re seeking something highly prescriptive with a traditional 9-to-5.

The Opportunity

Voice is the most natural modality for human interaction with machines. However, current sequence modeling paradigms based on jointly scaling model and data cannot deliver voice AI capable of universal human interaction. The challenges are rooted in fundamental data problems posed by audio: real-world audio data is scarce and enormously diverse, spanning a vast space of voices, speaking styles, and acoustic conditions. Even if billions of hours of audio were accessible, its inherent high dimensionality creates computational and storage costs that make training and deployment prohibitively expensive at world scale. We believe that entirely new paradigms for audio AI are needed to overcome these challenges and make voice interaction accessible to everyone.

The Role

As a Member of the Research Staff, you will pioneer the development of Latent Space Models (LSMs), a new approach that aims to solve the fundamental data, scale, and cost challenges associated with building robust, contextualized voice AI. Your research will focus on solving one or more of the following problems:

- Build next-generation neural audio codecs that achieve extreme, low bit-rate compression and high fidelity reconstruction across a world-scale corpus of general audio.

- Pioneer steerable generative models that can synthesize the full diversity of human speech from the codec latent representation, from casual conversation to highly emotional expression to complex multi-speaker scenarios with environmental noise and overlapping speech.

- Develop embedding systems that cleanly factorize the codec latent space into interpretable dimensions of speaker, content, style, environment, and channel effects -- enabling precise control over each aspect and the ability to massively amplify an existing seed dataset through “latent recombination”.

- Leverage latent recombination to generate synthetic audio data at previously impossible scales, unlocking joint model and data scaling paradigms for audio. Endeavor to train multimodal speech-to-speech systems that can 1) understand any human irrespective of their demographics, state, or environment and 2) produce empathic, human-like responses that achieve conversational or task-oriented objectives. 

- Design model architectures, training schemes, and inference algorithms that are adapted for hardware at the bare metal enabling cost efficient training on billion-hour datasets and powering real-time inference for hundreds of millions of concurrent conversations.

The Challenge

We are seeking researchers who:

- See "unsolved" problems as opportunities to pioneer entirely new approaches

- Can identify the one critical experiment that will validate or kill an idea in days, not months

- Have the vision to scale successful proofs-of-concept 100x

- Are obsessed with using AI to automate and amplify your own impact

If you find yourself energized rather than daunted by these expectations—if you're already thinking about five ideas to try while reading this—you might be the researcher we need. This role demands obsession with the problems, creativity in approach, and relentless drive toward elegant, scalable solutions. The technical challenges are immense, but the potential impact is transformative.

It's Important to Us That You Have

- Strong mathematical foundation in statistical learning theory, particularly in areas relevant to self-supervised and multimodal learning

- Deep expertise in foundation model architectures, with an understanding of how to scale training across multiple modalities

- Proven ability to bridge theory and practice—someone who can both derive novel mathematical formulations and implement them efficiently

- Demonstrated ability to build data pipelines that can process and curate massive datasets while maintaining quality and diversity

- Track record of designing controlled experiments that isolate the impact of architectural innovations and validate theoretical insights

- Experience optimizing models for real-world deployment, including knowledge of hardware constraints and efficiency techniques

- History of open-source contributions or research publications that have advanced the state of the art in speech/language AI

Ideal Researcher Profile

An ideal researcher, as evidenced by the recurring themes across these foundational papers, excels in five key areas: (1) Statistical & Mathematical Foundations, (2) Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation, (3) Data-Driven & Scalable Systems, (4) Hardware & Systems Understanding, and (5) Rigorous Experimental Design. Below is a synthesis of how each paper highlights these qualities, with references illustrating why they matter for building robust, impactful deep learning models.

1. Statistical & Mathematical Foundations 

Mastery of Core Concepts 

Many papers, like Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models and Neural Discrete Representation Learning (VQ-VAE), reflect the importance of power-law analyses, derivation of novel losses, or adaptation of fundamental equations (e.g., in VQ-VAE's commitment loss or rectified flows in Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers). Such mathematical grounding clarifies why models converge or suffer collapse.

Combining Existing Theories in Novel Ways 

Papers such as Moshi (combining text modeling, audio codecs, and hierarchical generative modeling) and Finite Scalar Quantization (FSQ's adaptation of classic scalar quantization to replace vector-quantized representations) show how reusing but reimagining known techniques can yield breakthroughs. Many references (e.g., the structured state-space duality in Transformers are SSMs) underscore how unifying previously separate research lines can reveal powerful algorithmic or theoretical insights.

Logical Reasoning and Assumption Testing 

Across all papers—particularly in the problem statements of Whisper or Rectified Flow Transformers—the authors present assumptions (e.g., "scaling data leads to zero-shot robustness" or "straight-line noise injection improves sample efficiency") and systematically verify them with thorough empirical results. An ideal researcher similarly grounds new ideas in well-formed, testable hypotheses.

2. Algorithmic Innovation & Implementation 

Creative Solutions to Known Bottlenecks 

Each paper puts forth a unique algorithmic contribution—Rectified Flow Transformers redefines standard diffusion paths, FSQ proposes simpler scalar quantizations contrasted with VQ, phi-3 mini relies on curated data and blocksparse attention, and Mamba-2 merges SSM speed with attention concepts.

Turning Theory into Practice 

Whether it's the direct preference optimization (DPO) for alignment in phi-3 or the residual vector quantization in SoundStream, these works show that bridging design insights with implementable prototypes is essential.

Clear Impact Through Prototypes & Open-Source 

Many references (Whisper, neural discrete representation learning, Mamba-2) highlight releasing code or pretrained models, enabling the broader community to replicate and build upon new methods. This premise of collaboration fosters faster progress.

3. Data-Driven & Scalable Systems 

Emphasis on Large-Scale Data and Efficient Pipelines 

Papers such as Robust Speech Recognition via Large-Scale Weak Supervision (Whisper) and BASE TTS demonstrate that collecting and processing hundreds of thousands of hours of real-world audio can unlock new capabilities in zero-shot or low-resource domains. Meanwhile, phi-3 Technical Report shows that filtering and curating data at scale (e.g., "data optimal regime") can yield high performance even in smaller models.

Strategic Use of Data for Staged Training 

A recurring strategy is to vary sources of data or the order of tasks. Whisper trains on multilingual tasks, BASE TTS uses subsets/stages for pretraining on speech tokens, and phi-3 deploys multiple training phases (web data, then synthetic data). This systematic approach to data underscores how an ideal researcher designs training curricula and data filtering protocols for maximum performance.

4. Hardware & Systems Understanding 

Efficient Implementations at Scale 

Many works illustrate how researchers tune architectures for modern accelerators: the In-Datacenter TPU paper exemplifies domain-specific hardware design for dense matrix multiplications, while phi-3 leverages blocksparse attention and custom Triton kernels to run advanced LLMs on resource-limited devices.

Real-Time & On-Device Constraints 

SoundStream shows how to compress audio in real time on a smartphone CPU, demonstrating that knowledge of hardware constraints (latency, limited memory) drives design choices. Similarly, Moshi's low-latency streaming TTS and phi-3-mini's phone-based inference highlight that an ideal researcher must adapt algorithms to resource limits while maintaining robustness.

Architectural & Optimization Details 

Papers like Mamba-2 in Transformers are SSMs and the In-Datacenter TPU work show how exploiting specialized matrix decomposition, custom memory hierarchies, or quantization approaches can lead to breakthroughs in speed or energy efficiency.

5. Rigorous Experimental Design 

Controlled Comparisons & Ablations 

Nearly all papers—Whisper, FSQ, Mamba-2, BASE TTS—use systematic ablations to isolate the impact of individual components (e.g., ablation on vector-quantization vs. scalar quantization in FSQ, or size of codebooks in VQ-VAEs). This approach reveals which design decisions truly matter.

Multifold Evaluation Metrics 

From MUSHRA listening tests (SoundStream, BASE TTS) to FID in image synthesis (Scaling Rectified Flow Transformers, FSQ) to perplexity or zero-shot generalization in language (phi-3, Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models), the works demonstrate the value of comprehensive, carefully chosen metrics.

title: Data Scientist
description:
Data Scientist | Semiconductor Metrology 
Abingdon, UK

Reward and Benefits 

- £42,000 - £55,000 (depending on experience)

- Annual bonus, 3x salary death in service benefit and private health care BUPA, EMI Share scheme.

If you are a Data Scientist who enjoys turning instrument data into proof of what is possible, why not join us in Abingdon, Oxfordshire, and help prove the analysis methods behind advanced semiconductor metrology systems.

We are looking for an ambitious and adaptable Data Scientist to join our new Data Science team in the Technology department, reporting to the Data Science Lead and working closely with our Modelling Scientist. You will generate and curate data, develop and test new algorithms, and benchmark them against what the instrument can physically deliver. When a method proves itself, you will package it for the Data Analysis team in Engineering, who turn it into robust product software. You will work with real customer use cases and wafer data from Applications Development, and proof-of-concept data from R&D.

We are an AI-first team, so you will use AI tools every day, while checking carefully what they produce. If your passion is speed, evidence and finding out what the data can really tell you, we’d love to hear from you.

What you’ll be doing 

- Generate synthetic data, and build and maintain the demo and performance data libraries

- Analyse instrument data to quantify noise and limitations, and help establish the information limit, meaning what is physically extractable from the instrument

- Develop and test new algorithms and analysis methods (for example PCA, percentile methods and machine learning) on real and synthetic data

- Benchmark methods against the information limit: achievable performance, measurement uncertainty, gauge R&R and drift contributors

- Write clean, reproducible prototype code with test data and expected performance, ready to hand over to Data Analysis, and build analysis tools used across the Technology department

- Use AI tools every day to code, explore, analyse and report faster, verify what they produce, and present your results to the team

Education and experience 

- Degree or above in Physics, Data Science, Applied Mathematics, Engineering or a similar subject, or [2] years’ relevant experience in data science or quantitative research

Skills and experience we’re looking for: 

- Data analysis in Python (NumPy, SciPy, pandas, scikit-learn or similar)

- Heavy, day-to-day use of AI tools in your technical work, such as coding assistants and LLMs, with the judgement to verify their outputs

- Image or signal processing, ideally on data from scientific instruments

- Statistics applied to measurement data: uncertainty, repeatability, noise and drift

- Machine learning methods, and how to validate them properly

- Clear, reproducible code and reports

- Explaining results to technical and non-technical colleagues

- Curious and adaptable, happy to work quickly and test ideas against the evidence

We’d love to see: 

- Atomic Force Microscopy or other nano-characterisation (SEM, FIB, profilometry), or semiconductor metrology

- Physics-based modelling or simulation

- Version control (Git) and C#, and experience building agentic or AI-assisted analysis workflows

A bit about us: 

Infinitesima is a privately owned company founded in 2001, as a spin-out of the University of Bristol, by CTO Professor Andrew Humphris. Our dynamic team of scientists and engineers is focussed on enabling the next generation of semiconductor devices through delivery of innovative products to customers around the world. 

Our strength lies in the varied perspectives that come from different cultures, experiences, and identities. We believe that true innovation is fuelled by collaboration, locally and globally. We strive to foster an environment where everyone can contribute meaningfully and thrive. If you require adjustments to take part in the recruitment process, please let us know, we’ll do our best to support you. 

Your recruitment journey: 

We will interview you: Monday to Friday UK Time 9am to 4.30pm and we'll be as flexible as we can with Global Scheduling 

1st stage: (45 minute) Remote meeting to evaluate your experience and technical ability 

2nd stage: (2.5 hours) Face to face onsite evaluating technical, presentation and communication skills along with your ways of working and your opportunity to to know more about us 

If you're not comfortable with eye contact, let us know at the start of your interview and if REMOTE, once we've said hello, feel free to turn your camera off until the end. 

We dress casually so informal attire is absolutely fine for onsite interviews. We want you to feel comfortable when you meet us and if there's anything else we can do to support your journey, just let us know. 

A note on how we use AI: 
We use AI only to transcribe our interviews so we can focus fully on you instead of scribbling notes. The AI does not take part in any decision making at any stage. All hiring decisions are made by real humans based on the conversation we have with you.

Location and working pattern:
We recognise the value of flexibility and offer a hybrid working model wherever possible. Most employees work onsite three days per week, although some positions require a greater onsite presence due to the nature of the work and business need

Recruitment agencies: Infinitesima Ltd only works with approved agencies and does not accept unsolicited agency CVs. Please do not submit candidate details in response to this advert or solicit any Infinitesima Ltd employees. Infinitesima Ltd is not responsible for any fees related to unsolicited CVs.

title: Partner Account Manager - France
description:
About Anthropic 

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

À propos du poste

Ce poste de direction est essentiel : il consiste à construire et à faire passer à l’échelle les partenariats d’Anthropic avec les cabinets de conseil, les intégrateurs de systèmes mondiaux (GSI) et les boutiques partenaires nativement IA en France.

Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec l’équipe commerciale pour que les clients adoptent l’IA grâce à nos partenaires.

Ce poste est un poste de construction, et non de gestion. Compte tenu du stade de développement d’Anthropic, nous recherchons un profil qui a déjà fait ses preuves en faisant passer des partenariats de zéro à des moteurs de revenus à grande échelle, un profil qui a bâti ces relations de A à Z, et non simplement hérité de relations existantes pour les gérer.

Responsabilités 

- Partenariats et exécution

- Vous collaborerez étroitement avec l’équipe commerciale pour comprendre comment les partenaires peuvent soutenir l’adoption de Claude par les clients.

- Vous accompagnerez les partenaires dans la création de solutions clients reproductibles, répondant à des cas d’usage précis dans de nombreux secteurs : services financiers, santé, distribution, industrie, secteur public et services professionnels.

- Performance et pilotage des indicateurs clés (KPI)

- Vous portez la responsabilité des indicateurs clés de performance et vous les pilotez : revenus influencés par les partenaires, livraison réalisée par les partenaires, nombre de personnes consultantes formées et certifiées.

- Chaque deal influencé par votre portefeuille de partenaires doit être conçu pour la réussite du client et la croissance de sa valeur à long terme. Vous définirez des critères de réussite pour les comptes communs, veillerez à la qualité de la mise en œuvre et de l’accompagnement à l’adoption, et mettrez en place des boucles de retour d’expérience favorisant l’amélioration continue.

- Vous rendrez compte de la santé des partenariats, de leur avancement et de leurs résultats commerciaux, en vous appuyant sur des analyses fondées sur les données.

- Développement du marché et construction de la marque

- Vous renforcerez la notoriété de la marque Anthropic en France grâce à des relations stratégiques avec les partenaires.

- Vous élaborerez et déploierez des stratégies de mise sur le marché (GTM) propres à chaque marché, adaptées aux pratiques commerciales et aux nuances culturelles locales.

- Vous composerez avec les enjeux locaux de réglementation, de conformité et de souveraineté des données.

- Vous créerez un avantage concurrentiel grâce aux capacités singulières des partenaires et à des propositions de valeur élaborées en commun.

Votre profil 

Ce poste pourrait vous convenir si vous réunissez les atouts suivants :

- Vous avez l’esprit d’initiative et le goût de construire : vous êtes à l’aise pour partir de zéro et créer des partenariats d’envergure.

- Vous maîtrisez l’anglais et le français.

- Vous comptez au moins 8 ans d’expérience dans les partenariats technologiques à destination des entreprises, idéalement dans le cloud, l’IA/ML ou les activités de plateforme.

- Vous avez une culture de la donnée, tournée vers les résultats mesurables et l’atteinte des KPI, et un historique avéré de revenus additionnels générés grâce aux partenariats dans la région.

- Vous avez démontré votre capacité à assurer la réussite des clients et la protection de la marque via les canaux partenaires.

- Vous avez l’esprit de compétition : la victoire et la différenciation sont votre moteur.

- Vous avez une approche collaborative et savez travailler de façon transversale avec les équipes commerciales, produit, marketing et régionales.

- Vous nourrissez une vraie passion pour l’IA et vous vous reconnaissez dans la mission d’Anthropic : développer une IA bénéfique.

Relations de travail 

Votre rattachement hiérarchique se fera auprès de la direction des partenariats internationaux, tandis que votre activité quotidienne sera pilotée par la personne responsable des partenariats EMEA Sud. Vous travaillerez également en étroite collaboration avec la direction commerciale régionale d’Anthropic et ses Account Executives, ainsi qu’avec les équipes Customer Success et Applied AI de la région.

Lieu et déplacements 

Ce poste est basé à Paris, en France, avec des déplacements à prévoir pour rencontrer les partenaires et les clients.

About the Role

This is a critical leadership role responsible for building and scaling Anthropic's consulting, GSIs and AI-native boutique partners in France.
You will be working closely with the sales team to make sure customers are adopting AI through our partners.

This is a builder role, not a manager role. Given Anthropic's stage, we need someone who has proven they can take partnerships from zero to scaled revenue engines — someone who has built these relationships from the ground up, not just inherited and managed existing ones.

Responsibilities: 

- Partnerships and execution: 

- You will engage closely with the sales team to understand how partners can support customer Claude adoption

- You will guide partners in creating repeatable customer solutions that address specific use cases across industries including financial services, healthcare, retail, manufacturing, public sector, and professional services.

- Performance and KPI ownership:

- Own and drive key performance indicators, partner-influenced revenue, partner delivery, consultants trained and certified

- Every deal influenced through your partner portfolio must be architected for customer success and long-term value expansion. You will establish success criteria for joint accounts, ensure proper implementation and adoption support, and create feedback loops that drive continuous improvement.

- Report on partnership health, progress, and commercial outcomes with data-driven insights

- Market Development & Brand Building

- Amplify the Anthropic brand in France strategic partner relationships

- Develop and execute market-specific GTM strategies adapted to local business practices and cultural nuances

- Navigate local regulatory, compliance, and data sovereignty considerations

- Create competitive differentiation through unique partner capabilities and joint value propositions

You may be a good fit if you have: 

- Builder mentality — comfortable starting from zero and creating scaled partnerships

Fluent in English and French 

- 8+ years of experience in enterprise technology partnerships, ideally within cloud, AI/ML, or platform businesses

- Data-driven mindset with focus on measurable outcomes and KPI attainment. Track record of driving incremental revenues through partnerships in the region

- History of delivering exceptional customer success and brand protection through partner channels

- Competitive drive — obsessed with winning and creating differentiation

- Collaborative approach with ability to work cross-functionally across sales, product, marketing, and regional teams

- Passion for AI and alignment with Anthropic's mission of beneficial AI development

Working Relationships 

You will formally report to the International Partnerships leader, while your day-to-day work will be led by our South EMEA Partnerships lead. You will also partner closely with Anthropic's regional sales leader and their Account Executives, as well as the in-region Customer Success and Applied AI teams.

Location and Travel 

This role will be based in Paris, France with travel expected to engage with partners and customers externally.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:

€220.000 — €260.000 EUR 

Logistics 

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

For roles performing work in California: We will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records or criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you ----- addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different 

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

title: Product Manager (Protocol)
description:
About Morpho

Morpho is a leading Decentralized Finance (DeFi) lending protocol backed by a16z crypto, Paradigm, Ribbit Capital, Apollo, Vaneck, Coinbase Ventures, Variant and 50 others to build an open credit network giving anyone, anywhere, access to the best possible terms. Morpho is experiencing exponential adoption, with over billion in deposits on the network and used by institutional clients including Bitwise, Galaxy, and Anchorage Digital and the largest crypto exchanges, such as Coinbase, Binance, and Kraken. Now, Morpho is scaling its team of contributors to establish itself as the open credit network, not just of DeFi, but of the world.

Why Morpho Exists

Everyone has the potential to build something great for the world. But fulfilling that ambition almost always requires more: people willing to trust you with their capital. Yet access to capital still depends on where you live, who you know, and which institutions are willing to trust you. Even when capital is available, it sits fragmented across disconnected networks and hidden behind intermediaries. The result is a system that fails most of the people it should serve. Borrowers overpay. Lenders earn less than they should. Many are shut out entirely, not because they are unworthy of credit, but because today's infrastructure was never built to connect them. Morpho exists to solve this. Full article here .

Location

Paris or remote (from -5h GMT up to +2h GMT to ensure sufficient overlap with the rest of the team).

Role

Morpho's Protocol team is evolving the core lending infrastructure that powers products and markets across the ecosystem. As the number of opportunities, integrations, and protocol initiatives grows, the team needs clear product direction on what to build, why it matters, and how to sequence the work. 

This role will work with Morpho’s protocol team to shape product strategy and guide execution. You will turn the needs of users and ecosystem partners into a focused roadmap, work closely with protocol and engineering teams to shape solutions, and drive improvements from discovery through launch and adoption. You will operate at the intersection of deeply technical systems, financial markets, and a fast-moving ecosystem.

Responsibilities

- Own the roadmap for Morpho's protocol team, defining the highest-impact problems to solve and sequencing opportunities against company goals, user needs, technical constraints, and ecosystem dynamics.

- Partner closely with protocol, engineering, research, security, legal, solutions, partnerships, and marketing to take initiatives from early exploration through design, implementation, audit, launch, and adoption.

- Evaluate product and technical tradeoffs, including when to extend the protocol, improve surrounding infrastructure, enable partners, or deliberately avoid adding complexity.

- Define and track the signals that show whether protocol initiatives are working, combining quantitative data with ecosystem feedback to guide iteration and future investment.

- Communicate product direction, decisions, tradeoffs, and release implications clearly to internal teams and external stakeholders.

- Improve how product decisions are made and documented as Morpho and its protocol ecosystem scale.

What Success Looks Like

First 30 days

You understand Morpho's protocol, development and release process, current roadmap, and the rationale behind the major initiatives in flight. You have built relationships across protocol, engineering, research, security, and go-to-market teams, and have started speaking with key curators, distributors, integrators, and developers.

First 3 months

You have established a clear, prioritized view of the most important protocol problems and opportunities. The roadmap reflects explicit tradeoffs, user evidence, technical constraints, and measurable outcomes. You have driven at least one meaningful initiative from discovery into execution and proactively keep stakeholders aligned on decisions and changes.

First 6 months

You have shipped a meaningful protocol improvement and can show how it advanced user or business outcomes. Product, protocol, and engineering teams have stronger shared context on what to build and why. You consistently identify important user needs, ecosystem shifts, and roadmap conflicts early, and have improved Morpho's product discovery and decision-making process.

Must Have Experience & Skills

- 5+ years building technical products in complex or fast-changing environments.

- Proven track record taking products or major features from ambiguous problem spaces through launch and iteration.

- Strong technical fluency, with the ability to reason about system design and constraints, engage deeply with engineers and researchers, and translate technical concepts for non-technical audiences.

- Excellent product judgment: you can distinguish important user problems from requests, make principled tradeoffs, and focus teams on the work with the greatest impact.

- Strong user discovery and synthesis skills, with the ability to uncover needs across different user types and turn incomplete or conflicting inputs into clear direction.

- Experience leading cross-functional work without relying on formal authority.

- Ability to define success, use quantitative and qualitative evidence, and adapt direction as new information emerges.

- Excellent written and verbal communication, especially in an async environment.

- Comfort creating clarity and driving decisions in highly ambiguous contexts.

- Strong ownership and autonomy: you act without waiting to be told.

- Team-first mindset, low ego.

Nice to Have

- Experience in crypto, DeFi, traditional finance, or fintech.

- Familiarity with lending markets, smart contracts, or permissionless protocols.

- Experience shipping products with significant security, audit, regulatory, or governance considerations.

- Experience working with research & development teams

title: Product Engineer
description:
Akur8 is one of the leading providers of insurance pricing and rating technology. Our mission is to modernize how insurers assess, price, and manage risk.

Our SaaS platform combines transparent machine learning, predictive analytics, and rating technology to turn complex insurance workflows into scalable, data-driven systems. Insurers use it to model and rate risk up to 10x faster while keeping transparency, explainability, and regulatory trust.

As the product suite expands, we are building an end-to-end platform for pricing, reserving, and forward-looking risk decisions.

Recognized globally, Akur8 has been featured in:

- CB Insights' Insurtech 50 (2025)

- CNBC's InsurTech Top 150 (2025)

- InsurTech100 Global Insurtech Top 100 (2025)

- Professional Equality Index 97/100 (2025)

Akur8 has 50+ nationalities across 8 global offices and serves 420+ clients across 4 continents. We’re an equal opportunities employer, and we value the different perspectives that help shape better products and decisions.

Insurance companies use Akur8 to decide the price of millions of policies. We are looking for a talented Product Engineer to build the features they rely on to do it. 

You will join the Pricing team, which builds the part of the Akur8 platform that Actuaries, Underwriters and Product Owners use to design, test and deploy their rates. Your mission is to scope, design and implement features that automate the rating process at insurance companies, from the first discussion of a client need to the feature running in production.

Much of the work is deciding what to build, not only building it. You will work with Product Managers, Designers, Actuaries and other Engineers to understand how insurers price risk, why they work the way they do, and where software can make them faster and more accurate. A good understanding of modelling, maths and logic is needed for this.

At its core, this is a hands-on software engineering role. You will spend significant time writing code, designing data models, building backend and frontend services, and ensuring the systems you ship are scalable, tested, and maintainable.

With AI being a reliable support for implementation, your main value will come from understanding the business context, the architecture and the data models as these will determine the quality of your deliveries. Our platform runs on AWS with Rust, Java, Python, and Angular. Prior experience with them is a plus.

You will work on the core of the platform from your first weeks and see the impact of your work on real clients.

In this role, you will: 

- Own product features end to end: clarify the need with the product team, scope it, design the solution, build it and follow it in production.

- Turn requests from Actuaries, Underwriters and Product Owners into a clear scope, and challenge a requirement when a simpler solution meets the need.

- Work in an AI native-engineering team: delegate implementation to deliver quickly, reviewing, test and own responsibility for everything you ship.

- Balance delivery speed and robustness according to the client’s priorities.

Your work will help insurers price risk faster and more accurately, and will expand what Akur8 can offer its clients. 

We’re looking for someone driven by outcomes: things done fast, done well, and useful to our clients. 

- You have completed or are finishing a PhD in Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Physics, or another quantitative field. No professional experience is required.

- You have written code during your research and want to grow in software engineering practices such as testing, code review and system design, using AI coding assistants as part of your daily work.

- You are comfortable with ambiguity: you can take a loosely defined problem, structure it and move it forward without waiting for a step-by-step brief.

- You take a pragmatic approach to writing code: you care about solving the actual problem rather than chasing perfection, and you can explain the trade-offs behind your technical choices.

- You care about results more than about technology: you want to understand why a feature matters to the end user before deciding how to build it.

Prior experience with our tech stack (Rust, Java, Python, Angular, AWS) or the insurance space is welcome, but not required. We invest heavily in onboarding; what matters most is your curiosity and appetite to learn.

Important : You must possess an employment status: French or Schengen area nationality or a ‘carte de séjour’ that will allow you to work from our Paris office. We are equally open to the visa sponsorship of non-EU candidates as long as they are already in possession of their final diploma / attestation of their final academic results. 

As a newcomer, you'll be joining a diverse, highly skilled and motivated team, with a strong Tech DNA, colleagues that are eager to share their knowledge and passion. 

But it’s not all work, you’ll also be part of a dynamic team that enjoys spending time together and having fun, including karaoke, team lunches, playing sports as well as the occasional ‘happy hour’.

In addition to this, we will provide you with:

- Relocation support

- Great office in the heart of the 9th arrondissement of Paris

title: Head of Internal Control, Operational Risk - CDI (F/H)
description:
Lemonway est un établissement de paiement européen agréé, qui accompagne les marketplaces et les plateformes de crowdfunding dans plus de 29 pays. 

Nous fournissons des services de paiement sécurisés, conformes et évolutifs pour la nouvelle économie, notamment des services de KYC, de traitement des paiements, de détection de la fraude, de ségrégation des fonds et de gestion des comptes. Notre expertise technologique et réglementaire permet à nos clients de développer leur activité tout en respectant les standards les plus exigeants en matière de conformité et de sécurité.

Avec plus de 150 collaborateurs, Lemonway est une entreprise dynamique et internationale, au cœur de l’économie numérique. Nous combinons l’agilité d’une scale-up avec les exigences et les responsabilités d’un établissement financier réglementé.

Le poste 

Rattaché(e) a notre Chief Compliance & Risk Officer, vous prenez en charge les activités de contrôle interne, de gestion des risques opérationnels et de gouvernance de Lemonway. 

Vous veillez à ce que le profil de risque de l’entreprise soit correctement identifié, évalué, suivi et communiqué, tout en contribuant au renforcement de son environnement de contrôle et de sa culture du risque.

Vous managez une équipe de deux personnes et travaillez en étroite collaboration avec le CEO, la Direction générale, les fonctions de contrôle et les équipes opérationnelles. En tant que véritable business partner, vous accompagnez l’entreprise dans ses prises de décision, tout en vous assurant que ses activités restent conformes aux exigences réglementaires applicables, aux politiques internes et à l’appétit au risque défini.

Il s’agit d’un poste stratégique et opérationnel, particulièrement adapté à une personne qui apprécie de construire et d’améliorer des dispositifs dans un environnement international, en forte évolution et réglementé.

Puisqu’il s’agit d’un poste centré sur la deuxième ligne de défense, nous recherchons des expériences en risques opérationnel et contrôle permanent au sein d’un établissement de paiement réglementé. Ce poste ne relève pas du contrôle financier, du FP&A, de la comptabilité, du contrôle de gestion ou du reporting financier.

Les principales responsabilités : 

Contrôle interne et contrôle permanent 

- Piloter et améliorer en continu le dispositif de contrôle interne de niveaux 1 et 2. 

- Définir, maintenir et mettre en œuvre le plan annuel de contrôle permanent. 

- Veiller à ce que les contrôles soient correctement conçus, documentés, réalisés et justifiés. 

- Développer les indicateurs de contrôle pertinents et les reportings destinés à la Direction et aux instances de gouvernance. 

- Identifier les faiblesses du dispositif de contrôle, évaluer leur impact et coordonner les actions correctives. 

- Promouvoir une culture forte du contrôle et de la gestion des risques dans l’ensemble de l’organisation. 

- Contribuer à la mise en place et à l’optimisation des outils et processus de type GRC.

Risques opérationnels et gestion des risques 

- Piloter le dispositif de gestion des risques opérationnels, notamment l’identification, l’évaluation et le suivi des risques. 

- Coordonner la préparation et la mise à jour régulière des cartographies des risques de l’entreprise. 

- Organiser et maintenir le Risk Appetite Framework, ainsi que le suivi des indicateurs d’appétit au risque. 

- Piloter le processus de gestion et de reporting des incidents, en veillant à ce que les incidents soient enregistrés, analysés et suivis de manière appropriée. 

- Suivre les risques opérationnels, non financiers et émergents, notamment les risques liés à la technologie, à la cybersécurité, à la fraude, à l’externalisation et aux processus métiers. 

- Préparer des reportings risques clairs et exploitables à destination de la Direction générale et des instances de gouvernance concernées.

Gouvernance et comités 

- Préparer, coordonner et animer le Comité des risques trimestriel. 

- Accompagner le Chief Compliance & Risk Officer et la Direction générale dans leurs prises de décision liées aux risques. 

- Préparer les supports de gouvernance, tableaux de bord et présentations offrant une vision claire de l’environnement de risques et de contrôle de l’entreprise. 

- Coordonner la définition et la mise à jour des rôles et responsabilités, notamment au travers des matrices RACI. 

- Contribuer aux processus de reporting réglementaire et interne, notamment au rapport annuel sur le contrôle interne, ainsi qu’aux autres reportings réglementaires applicables.

Audits et contrôles réglementaires 

- Coordonner les audits externes, réglementaires et internes portant sur le contrôle interne, les risques opérationnels et la gouvernance. 

- Être le point de contact principal des auditeurs et des autorités compétentes sur les sujets de contrôle interne. 

- Gérer les demandes d’audit, la collecte des éléments justificatifs, le suivi des constats et les actions associées. 

- Coordonner la préparation et la mise en œuvre des plans d’actions correctifs et préventifs. 

- Suivre l’avancement des plans de remédiation et présenter les actions à risque élevé ou en retard aux instances de gouvernance appropriées. 

- Coordonner le programme de contrôle périodique et suivre sa mise en œuvre conformément au plan d’audit défini.

Externalisation, continuité d’activité et résilience opérationnelle 

- Garantir la robustesse et la bonne exécution du dispositif PSEE. 

- Contribuer au pilotage des activités externalisées et des prestataires tiers, conformément aux exigences réglementaires applicables. 

- Piloter les activités de continuité d’activité et de résilience opérationnelle de l’entreprise. 

- Maintenir et tester régulièrement les plans de continuité d’activité. 

- Participer aux exercices et aux réunions de gestion de crise lorsque cela est nécessaire. 

- Identifier les opportunités permettant de renforcer la résilience de Lemonway et sa capacité à maintenir ses activités critiques en cas de perturbation.

Politiques, procédures et formation 

- Évaluer les besoins de création ou de mise à jour des politiques, procédures, formulaires et documents de contrôle. 

- Coordonner la rédaction, la revue et la mise en œuvre des procédures de contrôle interne et de gestion des risques. 

- Concevoir ou contribuer à la création de supports de formation et de sensibilisation. 

- Veiller à ce que la documentation soit claire, opérationnelle, à jour et alignée avec le modèle de fonctionnement de l’entreprise. 

Expérience 

- Vous disposez d’au moins 8 ans d’expérience dans le contrôle interne, les risques opérationnels, l’ERM, l’audit, la conformité ou un domaine proche. 

- Vous avez évolué dans un environnement réglementé, idéalement dans le secteur du paiement ou en fintech. 

- Vous avez déjà encadré une équipe et travaillé sur la structuration ou la transformation d’un dispositif de gestion des risques et de contrôle interne. 

Compétences recherchées 

- Solide connaissance des dispositifs de contrôle interne et de gestion des risques opérationnels. 

- Bonne compréhension de l’environnement réglementaire français et européen, notamment des attentes de l’ACPR, des orientations de l’EBA, des exigences LCB-FT et de la DSP2. 

- Expérience du fonctionnement d’instances de gouvernance et de la préparation de reportings destinés à la Direction générale. 

- Maîtrise des environnements de transformation, de croissance ou de scale-up. 

- Expérience de la mise en place ou de l’évolution d’outils GRC. 

- Très bon niveau de français et d’anglais, à l’écrit comme à l’oral. 

- La connaissance de l’allemand ou d’une autre langue européenne constitue un atout.

Qualités personnelles 

- Leadership affirmé et bonnes compétences managériales. 

- Esprit structuré, rigoureux et grande capacité d’organisation. 

- Autonomie, tout en appréciant le travail collaboratif. 

- Approche pragmatique, orientée solutions et résultats. 

- Solides capacités d’analyse et grande attention aux détails. 

- Excellentes compétences en communication et en gestion des parties prenantes. 

- Capacité à challenger de manière constructive et à convaincre des interlocuteurs de tous niveaux. 

Avantages 

- Bureaux au cœur du Sentier (Paris 2e) 

- Poste hybride (2j TT / semaine, et 3 semaines de full-remote par an) 

- Carte Swile

- Accès à Gymlib

title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer, PaaS
description:
Algolia is the retrieval intelligence layer that turns intent into trusted, decision-grade outcomes. Powering more than 1.7 trillion queries a year for over 18,000 customers with millisecond latency and 99.999% reliability, we are the recognized leader for Search and Product Discovery by top industry analyst firms. The Algolia platform turns a company's products, content, and business rules into data that humans, applications and AI agents can act upon. The result is trusted customer experiences with stronger conversions for measurable business impact. 

Algolia is set to enable every company to create world-class Search and Discovery experiences with an API-first approach. Performance and Scalability is at the heart of our mission: we power 1.5 trillion searches a year, for 10K+ customers all over the world. 

If you're a problem solver, able to think outside the box and eager to nurture others and learn from them, then this is your challenge!

The Team

The Platform as a Service (PaaS) team is dedicated to empowering development teams by creating toolchains, guidelines, and standards. Our focus is on enabling seamless automation and CI/CD, comprehensive observability, and unwavering reliability in a secured cloud-native environment.

The Opportunity

The Senior Site Reliability Engineer (IC4) position within the Platform As a Service team presents an exciting opportunity for a seasoned professional to enhance scalable infrastructure with a focus on CI/CD, Observability, and application hosting. In this role, you will bridge the gap between our junior and senior staff, playing a critical role in ensuring the reliability, scalability, and performance of Algolia’s Search Products.

As a senior contributor, you will be responsible for building and optimizing systems that ensure the platform’s efficiency and reliability, while also mentoring junior engineers and collaborating across teams. Your work will be pivotal in improving infrastructure, enhancing observability standards, and streamlining CI/CD processes. You will play a significant role in transitioning legacy systems to a modern Kubernetes-based architecture, contributing to long-term infrastructure strategies, and ensuring alignment with business needs.

Your role will consist of:

- 
CI/CD Development and Maintenance : Contribute to the design, optimization, and maintenance of the CI/CD pipelines to improve the speed, reliability, and efficiency of the development lifecycle. Assist in driving standardization across various services hosted on the platform.

- 
Observability Enhancement : Lead efforts to improve the observability of critical systems, working closely with cross-functional teams to ensure actionable monitoring and alerting frameworks are in place. Help troubleshoot complex issues and optimize system reliability.

- 
Kubernetes and Cloud Management : Contribute to the development and operation of our Kubernetes-based architecture. Ensure systems are resilient, scalable, and optimized for performance. Actively participate in enhancing cloud-based solutions for API management and microservices.

- 
System Optimization and Scaling : Collaborate with team members to ensure system scalability, operability, and performance. Lead initiatives to optimize resource utilization, focusing on cost efficiency while maintaining high system availability.

- 
Mentorship and Knowledge Sharing : Mentor mid-level engineers (IC3) by providing guidance on technical challenges and SRE best practices. Support team growth by fostering knowledge-sharing sessions and helping establish processes that drive operational excellence.

- 
Cross-Team Collaboration : Work closely with product, software, and other SRE teams to ensure that platform goals align with broader business objectives. Drive initiatives aimed at enhancing platform stability, security, and scalability.

You might be a fit if you have:

- 
Strong Programming Skills : Proficient in Golang and Python with a solid understanding of software craftsmanship. Knowledge of Ruby is a plus.

- 
Experience in CI/CD Pipelines : Hands-on experience in building and maintaining CI/CD pipelines using tools like GitHub Actions, CircleCI, or alternatives. Familiarity with best practices for ensuring build and deployment reliability.

- 
Observability : Experience designing and implementing monitoring, alerting, and observability frameworks that provide actionable insights. Strong troubleshooting skills in production environments.

- 
Kubernetes and Cloud Infrastructure : Proven experience in managing and optimizing Kubernetes-based architectures and working with public cloud providers such as GCP, AWS, or Microsoft Azure.

- 
Distributed Systems Expertise : Experience in designing, building, and operating distributed systems at scale, with a focus on reliability, availability, and performance.

- 
Mentorship and Leadership : Experience mentoring junior engineers and helping them grow. Ability to collaborate with cross-functional teams and contribute to strategic initiatives.

- 
Problem-Solving Skills : Ability to independently solve complex technical problems with minimal supervision while collaborating effectively with other team members.

- 
Excellent Communication and Organizational Skills : Strong ability to communicate complex technical issues to both technical and non-technical audiences. Ability to organize and prioritize multiple projects.

Algolia does not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, military status, veteran status, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by law.

The annual base salary compensation range for this role reflects market pay data within this location. The exact compensation offered for this role may vary depending on specific location and job-related knowledge, technical skills, and experience; and is only one part of our Total Rewards philosophy to compensate and recognize employees for their work.

Base Salary Pay Range

€69.768 — €96.900 EUR 

FLEXIBLE WORKPLACE STRATEGY: 

Algolia’s flexible workplace model is designed to empower all Algolians to fulfill our mission to power search and discovery with ease. We place an emphasis on an individual’s impact, contribution, and output, over their physical location. Algolia is a high-trust environment and many of our team members have the autonomy to choose where they want to work and when. 

We have a global presence with offices in Paris, NYC, London, Sydney and Bucharest, however we also offer many of our team members the option to work remotely either as fully remote or hybrid-remote employees. Positions listed as "Remote" are only available for remote work within the specified country. Positions listed within a specific city are only available in that location - depending on the role it may be available with either a hybrid-remote or in-office schedule. 

WE’RE LOOKING FOR SOMEONE WHO CAN LIVE OUR VALUES: 

- GRIT - Problem-solving and perseverance capability in an ever-changing and growing environment.

- TRUST - Willingness to trust our co-workers and to take ownership.

- CANDOR - Ability to receive and give constructive feedback.

- CARE - Genuine care about other team members, our clients and the decisions we make in the company.

- HUMILITY - Aptitude for learning from others, putting ego aside.

We’re looking for talented, passionate people to help build the world’s best search and discovery technology. We value autonomy, diversity, and collaboration. We’re committed to creating an inclusive workplace where everyone is respected and supported—regardless of race, age, ancestry, religion, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, marital status, color, veteran status, disability, or socioeconomic background.

IMPORTANT NOTICE FOR CANDIDATES - Recruitment Fraud Notice

READY TO APPLY? 

If you share our values and our enthusiasm for building the world’s best search & discovery technology, we’d love to review your application!
