title: Senior Partner Solutions Architect (Pan-EMEA GSI)
description:
The Team: 

We are Datadog's in-house product experts. The technical solutions team enables Datadog's worldwide growth by educating potential clients and ensuring that existing customers are happy and successful. We share our technical and product expertise with customers through demos, presentations, technical evaluations, and ongoing support. Technical solutions is a growing global team that collaborates constantly to share knowledge and continuously advance our technical skillset.

The Opportunity: 

The Partner Solution Architect (PSA) is a Datadog expert who will work closely with Datadog’s Director, Adoption Services, and is aligned to our Channels & Alliances business segment. The PSA is responsible for supporting a variety of technical initiatives and activities for our partners (for example: cloud migration, application modernization, DevOps transformation). They are accountable for the outcome of these initiatives, and frequently collaborate with both Datadog and Partner resources to drive success. The PSA is a trusted technical advisor for our Partner channel.

You Will: 

- Ensure the successful onboarding, training, enablement, and certification of partner technical resources;

- Participate in periodic joint business planning and review sessions to ensure direct alignment between Datadog and Partner technical teams;

- Collaborate internally to support Partner technical initiatives such as end-customer demonstrations and proofs of value; partner team enablement workshops; assessment, advice, and coaching on lead practices;

- Advocate on behalf of Partners’ technical concerns (use cases, feature requests, support issues, e.g.) with Datadog internal teams and personnel, helping to bring those concerns to resolution;

- Analyze and understand Partner service offerings on a regular basis and provide recommendations to enhance the value of those services through greater or improved adoption of Datadog features and capabilities;

- Collaborate with Datadog’s product management, engineering and technical services teams to help identify and prioritize new features and capabilities;

- Continuously help curate and evolve lead/best practices for Datadog platform adoption and success.

You Are: 

- Possess a solid technical grounding with hands-on experience of IT Development and/or Operations;

- A demonstrable track-record and never-ending passion for learning;

- A self-starter, tech-savvy professional with solid business acumen; ability to articulate Datadog value from server room to boardroom;

- Confident presentation skills;

- Must be a current EU resident

- Desired hands-on experience in two or more of the following areas:

- Observability: Datadog, Splunk, AppD, New Relic or Dynatrace

- Public Cloud: AWS, Azure, GCP, or Alibaba

- Containerization: Docker, Kubernetes, OpenShift, Cloud Foundry

- Dev/Scripting: Python, Javascript, Ruby, Perl, PHP, Go

- Config Mgmt: Terraform, Ansible, Puppet, Chef

- CI / CD: Jenkins, Gitlab

Bonus Points: 

- Previous experience working in a technical role for or supporting channel partners (Systems Integrators, Managed Services Providers, e.g.);

- Previous experience using Datadog and/or other cloud monitoring tools (APM, Infrastructure, Logs, Synthetics, NPM);

- Previous experience with root-cause-analysis, troubleshooting, debugging

Why You Should Apply: 

- Generous and competitive global and US benefits 

- New hire stock equity (RSUs) and employee stock purchase plan

- Continuous career development and pathing opportunities 

- Product training to develop an in-depth understanding of our product and space

- Best in breed onboarding

- Internal mentor and buddy program cross-departmentally

- Friendly and inclusive workplace culture

About Datadog: 

Datadog is the monitoring and security platform for cloud applications. Our SaaS product is used by organizations of all sizes across a wide range of industries to enable digital transformation, cloud migration, and infrastructure monitoring of our customers’ entire technology stack, allowing for seamless collaboration and problem-solving among Dev, Ops and Security teams globally. Given the resilience of cloud technologies and importance placed today in digital operations and agility, Datadog continues to innovate and is well positioned for the long term.

#LI-Remote

About Datadog: 

Datadog is the leading observability and security platform for the AI era, providing businesses with unified visibility across the technology stack to manage complexity at scale. It brings applications, infrastructure, data, models, and security into one place, using AI to detect and resolve issues before they impact customers. Trusted globally by Fortune 500 companies and high-growth AI leaders, Datadog enables businesses to move faster with clarity and confidence. Learn more about #DatadogLife on Instagram , LinkedIn, and Datadog Learning Center.

title: Senior DevOps Engineer
description:
At Ledgy, we’re on a mission to make Europe a powerhouse of entrepreneurship by building a modern, tech-driven equity management and financial reporting platform for private and public companies. In 2026, we aim to be the leading provider for European IPOs and reporting for share-based payments. We are a value-based company with a core focus on being humble, transparent, ambitious and impactful, all in order to delivery the best experience for our customers and end users.

We are proud to partner with some of the world’s leading investors. New Enterprise Associates led our $22m Series B round in 2022, with Philip Chopin joining Sequoia’s Luciana Lixandru on our board.

We were founded in Switzerland in 2017 and today we operate globally from offices in Zurich and London. We encourage diversity and are an international team coming from 26 different countries and speaking 25 different languages.

About the Role

As a Senior DevOps Engineer at Ledgy, you'll build the infrastructure and tooling that help our engineers ship quickly and reliably. You'll join our Platform team, collaborating with engineers and InfoSec to improve CI/CD, observability, and cloud infrastructure for a product that helps companies manage equity.

Our challenge is to make delivery faster, production easier to operate, and AI-assisted development safer - while keeping complexity and costs in check.

Location: We hire remotely across Spain, Germany, Poland, and Romania.

The team you'll join: Platform - Builds the infrastructure and tooling that help our engineers ship quickly and reliably, working with InfoSec to improve CI/CD, observability, and cloud infrastructure.

What You'll Work On

- Cloud infrastructure. Evolve our GCP and Kubernetes cloud architecture and setup with Terraform, improving reliability, simplicity, and cost visibility and enabling scaling to multiple availability regions.

- CI/CD and developer experience. Speed up feedback loops, reduce flaky builds, and turn recurring support requests into self-service tooling.

- Observability. Reduce alert noise, define meaningful SLOs, and make production issues easier to diagnose.

- Security and automation. Partner with InfoSec on secure delivery, access controls, and guardrails for AI-assisted workflows.

You'll also join our incident-response on-call rotation during working hours and help prevent recurring issues. As we expand our servicing of public companies and jurisdictions, this on-call might evolve to compensated 24h/7 hour rotation.

You'll Thrive in This Role If You

Don't worry if you don't tick every box. These are the things that would make you an especially good fit.

- Have strong DevOps / SRE background designing and operating cloud infrastructure and production systems

- Have worked with Kubernetes and infrastructure as code, ideally GCP and Terraform

- Enjoy building fast, reliable CI/CD pipelines and improving developer experience

- Can diagnose issues across networking, infrastructure, and application code

- Write maintainable code and bring a practical approach to observability and security

- Value collaboration, mentorship, and thoughtful trade-offs between reliability, complexity, and cost

- Are curious about supporting AI-assisted development safely - no AI specialism required

Experience with Node.js, MongoDB or Temporal is a plus.

Our Tech Stack

We work in TypeScript: React, Tailwind CSS, and tRPC on the front end, and tRPC, Node.js, MongoDB, and Temporal on the back end. Infrastructure runs on GCP, Terraform Cloud, Kubernetes, Docker, and GitHub Actions. For observability and incident response we use Grafana, Sentry, and PagerDuty.

You don't need to know all of it. We don't expect proficiency in every part of this stack. Strong infrastructure fundamentals and the ability to learn matter more than knowing every tool already.

What Your Journey Could Look Like

First 30 days: 

- Get to know Ledgy, the Platform team, and our internal users with an onboarding buddy

- Explore our infrastructure and delivery workflows, and ship your first improvement

- Analyze current state of our cloud infrastructure and propose meaningful enhancements

First 3 months: 

- Independently deliver improvements to CI/CD, observability, or infrastructure design

- Share operational ownership and help reduce recurring friction for engineers

- Contribute to architecture discussions and document what others need to operate our systems

First 6-12 months: 

- Own DevOps and SRE function and DevOps initiatives from problem definition through rollout and adoption

- Deliver measurable improvements to developer experience, reliability, or cost

- Help shape our platform's direction and mentor other engineers

The interview process

- Getting to know you (45 min): Meet with someone from our people team to talk about your experience and to ask questions about the role

- Live Coding (60 min): An equity domain problem to solve collaboratively using your preferred language and IDE. We want to see how you think, so this step does not allow AI. But you can freely look up syntax questions if you need to.

- System Design (60 min): A system design session where you will design an architecture for a problem from the Ledgy domain using a visual tool of your choice

- DDSA (45 min): A Deep Dive into real System Architecture that you have built, owned and monitored.

- Culture Interview: A chance to meet one of our founders and your hiring manager for a 30-minute chat about Ledgy's mission and values

- Offer 🎉

Being part of Ledgy means

- Recharge and re-energize with flexible working hours, 25 days of vacation, and up to 40 days of remote work from outside your home country.

- We make space for your own professional development, with a generous yearly learning & development budget.

- This role will receive a competitive salary + benefits + equity. All salaries are aligned with competitively benchmarked ranges based on work location and levelling.

title: Senior Director, Sales- DACH
description:
The Senior Director, Sales — DACH is a senior first-line sales leadership role responsible for building and driving a high-performing team of Strategic Account Executives focused on net-new logo acquisition and expansion across enterprise accounts in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland (DACH). This leader owns a significant ARR target and is accountable for the full sales cycle — from pipeline creation through close — within the DACH region. 

This is a high-visibility, high-impact role that sits at the intersection of enterprise sales leadership and DACH market GTM strategy. You will translate Talkdesk’s business objectives into a regional execution plan, serve as a brand ambassador for the Talkdesk CX platform, and partner closely with Marketing, Product, Channel, and Customer Success to drive durable growth across this strategic European market. 

DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES 

Team Leadership & Coaching 

- 
Lead and manage a team of DACH-based Strategic Account Executives focused on net-new and expansion opportunities across enterprise accounts in the region. 

- 
Coach, mentor, and develop AEs to drive high-quality pipeline creation, deal execution, and quota attainment across DACH-specific buying cycles and regional market nuances. 

- 
Foster a performance culture grounded in accountability, high empathy, and genuine investment in individual career progression. 

- 
Partner with Sales Enablement to ensure the team is skilled on Talkdesk messaging, competitive positioning, and AI capabilities tailored to the DACH market. 

Revenue & Strategy Ownership 

- 
Own regional DACH strategy and planning, ensuring customer retention, net-new growth, and expansion across core Talkdesk solutions — AI-powered contact center, customer experience automation, and workforce engagement management. 

- 
Use a data-driven approach to territory design, forecasting accuracy, and pipeline development aligned to Talkdesk’s consumption-based pricing model, adapted for local business practices in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. 

- 
Translate Talkdesk’s business objectives into a regional DACH execution strategy, ensuring alignment with broader European and corporate goals. 

- 
Build and maintain a healthy, predictable pipeline (3–4x coverage) and deliver accurate monthly and quarterly forecasts to senior leadership. 

Executive Engagement & Brand 

- 
Actively engage with executive stakeholders at key DACH accounts; lead strategic sales meetings, attend QBRs, and build trusted long-term relationships across a localized enterprise client portfolio. 

- 
Serve as a brand ambassador for Talkdesk, championing our CX vision and differentiating against CCaaS competitors across the DACH market. 

- 
Represent Talkdesk at local industry events, conferences, and customer forums relevant to the DACH region. 

Cross-Functional Partnership 

- 
Collaborate closely with Marketing, Product, Channel, and Customer Success to craft localized go-to-market campaigns, product feedback loops, and customer success programs tailored to the needs of the DACH enterprise customer base. 

- 
Develop and maintain deep fluency in the Talkdesk solution portfolio — including AI/automation capabilities and key ecosystem integrations (CRM, WFM, and region-specific platforms) — as well as the broader European CCaaS landscape. 

- 
Provide competitive intelligence and market feedback to Product, Marketing, and GTM leadership to inform roadmap, localized product requirements, and positioning decisions. 

QUALIFICATIONS 

Experience 

- 
5+ years in a senior customer-facing sales leadership role directly managing teams in the DACH region. 

- 
Proven success leading teams selling to DACH enterprise accounts, with strong command of local, complex, multi-stakeholder buying cycles, European procurement processes, and regional data privacy requirements (e.g., GDPR). 

- 
Experience working for a global B2B SaaS company that has scaled successfully through rapid growth, ideally establishing a strong foothold in Central Europe. 

- 
Demonstrated track record of exceeding regional ARR targets, including net-new logo acquisition and expansion, in complex European enterprise environments. 

- 
Experience with 6- and 7-figure ACV deal cycles; proficiency with enterprise sales methodologies (MEDDIC, MEDDPICC, or equivalent) preferred. 

- 
Familiarity with CCaaS, CX technology, or adjacent platforms (UCaaS, AI/automation, WFM) strongly preferred. 

- 
Language skills: Native-level or completely fluent written and spoken German, and professional fluency in English. 

Leadership & Team Building 

- 
Excellent people management skills — high empathy, strong consideration for local workplace cultures, and genuine commitment to individual career progression. 

- 
Experience building and scaling world-class local sales teams, including hiring, onboarding, and structured enablement across the DACH market. 

- 
Demonstrated ability to coach AEs through complex, multi-threaded deals and develop talent at all levels of the team. 

Competencies 

- 
Strong command of consumption-based and SaaS pricing models; ability to translate Talkdesk’s value proposition into compelling business outcomes for DACH enterprise clients. 

- 
Understanding of the development and implementation of large-scale, mission-critical enterprise applications. 

- 
Exceptional executive communication, presence, and relationship-building skills in both German and English business contexts. 

- 
Ability to operate with speed and clarity in a high-growth, fast-moving environment across a dynamic regional market. 

YOU’LL THRIVE AT TALKDESK IF… 

- 
You lead from the front — you’re in the deals, coaching in real time, and setting the standard for how the team sells in DACH. 

- 
You hold yourself and others accountable without losing the culture — direct, fair, and outcomes-focused. 

- 
You’re a builder — energized by growing a regional team, opening new accounts, and winning across the DACH market. 

- 
You thrive in ambiguity and bring a clear point of view, even when the European regulatory and competitive landscape is complex or shifting. 

- 
You operate with speed, cultural intelligence, and intellectual curiosity, and you don’t let regional nuances slow you down.

Our global team of courageous innovators is customer-obsessed, building AI-first solutions that put empathy, trust, and transparency at the center of every interaction. title: Director, Commissioning, EMEA
description:
Director, Commissioning, EMEA 

Role Summary 

The Commissioning Director, EMEA will lead commissioning across STACK data centre projects, from early project engagement through testing, validation and final power and facilities handover. This role provides programme-level leadership for the planning, development and consistent execution of commissioning activities across mission-critical facilities, ensuring systems perform safely, reliably and in line with design intent and client requirements.

Working across engineering, construction, operations and external commissioning partners, you will set and maintain commissioning standards, oversee test strategies and documentation, and provide clear visibility of progress, risk and readiness across the EMEA portfolio.

Key Responsibilities 

· Lead the development and execution of commissioning plans across STACK EMEA projects, including all commissioning levels through Integrated Systems Testing and handover.

· Develop, standardise and review commissioning documentation, including Functional Performance Tests, Factory Acceptance Tests, equipment start-up procedures, installation checklists, test protocols, scripts and methods.

· Ensure commissioning documentation and activities align with project design, specifications, Basis of Design and Owner’s Project Requirements.

· Provide programme-level oversight of multi-discipline pre-commissioning and commissioning activities across critical infrastructure construction and special projects.

· Coordinate with project teams, client engineers and technical stakeholders to assess issues identified during testing, determine criticality and drive appropriate resolution.

· Oversee QA/QC of pre-functional and functional test results, ensuring completeness, accuracy and appropriate interpretation of results.

· Provide commissioning input into project design, planning and schedules, identifying risks, dependencies and potential constraints early.

· Ensure commissioning activities comply with applicable safety, environmental, quality and technical standards, and actively support STACK safety programmes.

· Manage and coordinate commissioning agents and subcontractors on site, escalating issues or potential blockers that could affect project delivery.

· Track commissioning progress against key delivery milestones and provide programme reporting, metrics and data-driven insight to stakeholders.

· Partner with Procurement, Legal, Finance and other functions to develop effective cross-functional processes and resolve delivery gaps.

· Manage commissioning budgets and support effective commercial oversight of commissioning activities.

What You’ll Bring 

· Demonstrable commissioning leadership experience within data centres or other mission-critical environments, with strong experience managing complex mechanical and electrical commissioning programmes.

· A qualification in Electrical, Mechanical, Computer Engineering or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

· Strong technical knowledge of mechanical and electrical plant and services supporting mission-critical Data Centre environments, including MV/LV distribution switchgear, automatic transfer schemes, standby generators, UPS, chillers, CRAC/CRAH systems, ancillary cooling plant, BMS and automation/monitoring systems.

· Advanced understanding of mechanical and/or electrical systems commissioning, controls and design principles.

Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs. 

🚀 Our Story

Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.

Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.

Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists and AI at Partly .

🖍️ This role

This is a forward-deployed solutions role at the front line of Partly's European expansion. You'll be the technical engine behind new-market deals across the UK and the Nordics, turning messy real-world problems into signed pilots and putting genuinely differentiated AI in front of the people who run the repair industry.

Here's what you'd be working with. Partly runs two connected layers. Partly.com is the infrastructure platform, the B2B layer that powers parts data, cataloging, and procurement across hundreds of integrations globally. Partly.ai is the AI tool for repairers, built on top of that infrastructure, that makes finding and sourcing the right part feel like magic. Both are powered by Interpreter, Partly's proprietary foundation model for understanding automotive parts at scale, trained on licensed OEM build data across 52+ manufacturer agreements and continuously sharpened by feedback from thousands of users across our global network. No general-purpose AI model comes close on parts accuracy, and that is what makes agentic procurement automation possible at the precision the repair industry demands.

Your job is to deploy that into markets we haven't cracked yet. Automotive data is scattered around the world in complex, inconsistent formats, and the interesting work is in unifying it into something that drives a customer's business. You'll sit between Sales, Product, and Engineering, resolving the technical blockers that stand between a prospect and a deal, building demos and experimental features that show off what Interpreter can do, and shaping how the product gets built for and applied to each new market.

Why join now: Partly closed a $50M Series B at a $500M valuation and is scaling fast across the UK, Europe, the U.S., and Australasia, in a $1.9 trillion industry that has barely been touched by modern software. You'd be early, close to the founders and the model, and given real ownership from day one. If you like ambiguity, owning a problem end to end, and being the person who makes a deal technically possible with frontier AI, this role is built for you.

💻 What will you do

- Unblock new-market deals end to end. Own the technical path from first conversation to a signed pilot across the UK and the Nordics: scope integrations, map end-to-end estimating and parts workflows, and, together with the Commercial team, clear whatever stands between a prospect and a yes.

- Build integrations that make pilots possible. Stand up and debug the connections customers depend on (for example, the CABAS estimating integration for Nordic customer pilots or quick custom interfaces for client-facing demos), working close to the data and the code to get them live in test and beyond.

- Build demos and experimental features. Create market demos and portal prototypes that prove what Partly can do before committing core engineering, iterating fast on what prospects react to.

- Run Technical Readiness Assessments. Produce the TRAs that map a customer's systems and dependencies so both sides know exactly what a pilot requires.

- Turn data into a commercial case. Build value proposition frameworks, calculators, and reporting (for example, insurer reporting dashboards) that show customers the value in their own numbers.

- Be the voice of the UK and Nordics customer to Product. Translate recurring deal blockers into clear, prioritized product asks, and shape how the product gets built and applied for each new market.

- Work cross-functionally to hit deadlines. Coordinate across Sales, Product, and Engineering to solve customer problems and keep deals moving.

Want to learn more about the problems we're solving and the culture we're building at Partly? Hear directly from our team here: https://shorturl.at/iAFUX 

🥷 Your skills

- Comfortable working close to data and code, with the ability to review it independently. You can write SQL, read and debug your way around a codebase, and stand up demos or prototypes yourself rather than waiting on Engineering.

- Strong technical problem solver and systems thinker. You break ambiguous, messy problems into root causes and generalizable solutions, not one-off fixes.

NewOrbit builds satellites that fly in very low Earth orbit, below 300 km, along with the electric propulsion that keeps them there.

Flying closer to Earth means sharper imagery from smaller optics, and an orbit that cleans itself: our satellites de-orbit within a month at end of life, leaving no debris.

Our AURA family of RF gridded ion thrusters powers our own NEO-1 satellite, with first flight planned for Q3 2028, and is also offered to other operators.

Electric propulsion is what lets our satellites hold very low orbits, and our AURA RF gridded ion thruster is at the centre of it.

Hiring now 

We are hiring as soon as possible. This role is for someone who has already graduated, or who will complete their degree in time to start with us very soon. We are not able to consider final-year students who graduate in summer 2027 or later, and this is not a graduate scheme with a fixed annual intake.

Role Overview 

This is a first full-time engineering role on the NEO-1 satellite. You will design satellite hardware and help keep the satellite's full CAD assembly organised as the design matures, learning from our lead designer and working in a small, multidisciplinary team. You will take ownership of real parts early, translate requirements into manufacturable designs and support their validation through prototyping and environmental testing.

- Design and develop mechanical hardware for the satellite, such as brackets, panels, component mounts, thermal-control hardware and cable and harness routing, with guidance from the lead designer.

- ElevenAPI gives developers access to our leading AI audio foundational models.

Everything we do is the result of the creativity and commitment of our team - builders doing the best work of their lives. We are researchers, engineers, and operators. IOI medalists and ex-founders. If you want to work hard and create lasting positive impact, we want to hear from you.

How we work

- High-velocity: Rapid experimentation, lean autonomous teams, and minimal bureaucracy.

- Impact not job titles: We don’t have job titles. Instead, it’s about the impact you have. No task is above or beneath you.

- AI first: We use AI to move faster with higher-quality results. We do this across the whole company—from engineering to growth to operations.

- Excellence everywhere: Everything we do should match the quality of our AI models.

- Global team: We prioritize your talent, not your location.

What we offer

- Innovative culture: You’ll be part of a generational opportunity to define the trajectory of AI, surrounded by a team pushing the boundaries of what’s possible.

- Growth paths: Joining ElevenLabs means joining a dynamic team with countless opportunities to drive impact - beyond your immediate role and responsibilities.

- Learning & development : ElevenLabs proactively supports professional development through an annual discretionary stipend.

- Social travel : We also provide an annual discretionary stipend to meet up with colleagues each year, however you choose.

- Co-working : If you’re not located near one of our main hubs, we offer a monthly co-working stipend.

The right person has done this before at scale - at a company that grew fast and hired harder. Your team will look to you not just for direction, but as someone they can genuinely learn from. This will be an opportunity to shape the direction of Talent at ElevenLabs; where we go, how we get there and who we get there with. If you want to shape the future of the Talent industry by building industry-defining playbooks using the latest technology and AI solutions, whilst building an expert team - this might be your best fit yet.

In this role you will:

- Lead the full talent function across Research, GTM, Engineering & Product, and G&A hiring - setting strategy, managing team performance, building a recruiter capacity engine, and driving outcomes across all verticals.

- Responsible for owning the scope of Talent Operations in partnership with the Talent Operations Lead: ATS (Ashby) configuration, headcount tracking, hiring velocity metrics, and recruiter tooling - ensuring the function runs with precision and minimal friction.

- Identify innovative ways of approaching Talent: design the next-gen Talent org structure, envision how Talent processes can be agentified and work with the team to build ElevenLabs products throughout.

- Act as a strategic partner to department heads and hiring managers, bringing market intelligence, pipeline health visibility, and honest counsel on what it takes to consistently win the best people in the market.

- Build and maintain a strong talent brand through thoughtful candidate experience, community engagement, building a Talent events program and creative sourcing strategies.

- Coach and develop a team of recruiters, establishing clear standards for quality of hire, speed, and candidate experience.

- Partner with functional leaders across Research, Engineering, GTM, and Operations - acting as a trusted advisor who can challenge, align, and mobilize leaders around talent priorities and workforce strategy.

description:
About Us 

At LangChain, our mission is to make intelligent agents ubiquitous. We build the foundation for agent engineering in the real world, helping developers move from prototypes to production-ready AI agents that teams can rely on. We began as widely adopted open-source tools and have grown to also offer a platform for building, evaluating, deploying, and operating agents at scale.

With $125M raised at Series B from IVP, Sequoia, Benchmark, CapitalG, and Sapphire Ventures, we’re at a stage where we’re continuing to develop new products, growth is accelerating, and all team members have meaningful impact on what we build and how we work together. LangChain is a place where your contributions can shape how this technology shows up in the real world.

Today, our platform includes LangSmith (Observability, Evaluation, Deployment, Fleet, and Sandboxes), our open source frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, and Deep Agents), and the newly launched LangSmith Engine for autonomous agent improvement. We have 100M+ monthly open source downloads, 6,000+ active LangSmith customers, and 5 of the Fortune 10 use LangSmith in production (+ 35% of the Fortune 500 overall), including teams at Klarna, Clay, Coinbase, Workday, Lyft, Cloudflare, Harvey, Rippling, Vanta, LinkedIn, Monday.com, Nvidia, and Bridgewater.

About the Team:

The Professional Services team is the bridge between LangChain's technology and the enterprise customers building on top of it. We partner with some of the world's most ambitious companies to help them move from pilot to production — designing solutions, accelerating time-to-value, and ensuring teams get the most out of LangChain, LangGraph, and LangSmith. We work at the intersection of deep technical expertise and customer partnership, and we take pride in the outcomes our customers achieve. As LangChain grows, PS plays a direct role in shaping how enterprise AI gets built in the real world.

About the Role:

We're looking for an Engagement Manager to join our Professional Services team. You'll manage multiple concurrent technical engagements, ensuring successful delivery of Professional Services projects for enterprise customers. You'll be the primary point of contact for customers and coordinate cross-functional teams to deliver exceptional outcomes.

This role offers direct impact on customer success, the opportunity to shape processes and methodologies, and the chance to work with cutting-edge AI technology. You'll join a collaborative team environment with a strong engineering culture.

Location: This role can be based in our San Francisco or New York office. Employees within commuting distance work from the office five days per week. Candidates who live outside commuting distance (e.g. >1hr each way) may be eligible for hybrid arrangements depending on location and role requirements. Open to remote candidates within the US.

What You'll Do:

- Engagement Lifecycle Management: Manage the full engagement lifecycle from SOW review through closeout, including planning, execution, risk management, scope management, and handoff

- Customer Communication & Relationship Management: Serve as the primary point of contact for customers — deliver status updates, manage expectations, handle escalations, and negotiate scope changes

- Multi-Engagement Management: Manage 5–8 concurrent technical engagements simultaneously while maintaining quality and meeting deadlines

- Cross-Functional Coordination: Coordinate with Solution Architects, AI Engineers, Sales, Support, Enablement, and Product/Engineering teams; manage resource allocation and capacity planning

- Risk & Issue Management: Proactively identify risks and issues, develop mitigation strategies, track resolution, and ensure deliverables meet quality standards

What You'll Bring:

- You have 5+ years of engagement or project management experience, preferably with technical or software engagements

- You've managed multiple concurrent engagements and know how to keep quality high across all of them

- You have strong experience working with enterprise customers and leading customer-facing communication

- You've coordinated cross-functional technical teams — engineers, architects, product — and managed resource allocation

- You're experienced with project management tools such as Linear, Jira, Asana, or similar

- You've handled scope change management and complex stakeholder dynamics

- You have start-up DNA: you thrive in fast-paced, ambiguous environments and don't wait to be told what to do

- You're a natural communicator — clear, direct, and effective with both technical teams and executive stakeholders

You exemplify our operating principles 

- You are motivated to build something great: you hold a high bar for quality, craft, and impact

- You embrace hot takes: you share informed opinions, challenge the status quo, and engage in constructive debate

- You operate with maximum agency: you take ownership, move work forward independently, and help others unblock

- You run to the roar: you lean into hard problems, ambiguity, and fast-moving challenges

Nice to Have:

- PMP or similar project management certification

- Experience in Professional Services or consulting

- Experience with AI/ML or infrastructure engagements

- Experience with time tracking and billing coordination

- Knowledge of software development lifecycle and agile methodologies

Compensation Philosophy: 

We offer competitive compensation that includes base salary, variable compensation for relevant roles, meaningful equity, benefits, and perks. 

We are hiring for this role across a range of scope, and the compensation band reflects that. Your offer depends on what we learn about your impact, craft, leadership, and communication during the interview process. Team members in the EU, UK, and APAC receive locally competitive benefits aligned with regional norms and regulations.

Benefits

Benefits include medical, dental, and vision coverage, flexible vacation, a 401(k) plan, meals on in-office days in the US and more.

title: Machine Learning Engineer
description:
About the role 

Linkup is the web search engine built for AI. Our infrastructure crawls, indexes and serves the live web to AI agents, and it’s scaling fast.

We’re looking for a top‑tier Machine Learning Engineer to join Linkup and work hand‑in‑hand with our CTO, Denis Charrier , and the rest of the tech team.

Your core responsibilities will be to:
Design, train and ship ranking and retrieval models for AI agents

- Design, train and ship ranking and retrieval models for AI agents

- Bring new ranking signals into the engine, beyond pure relevance

- Build the evaluation framework that tells us what really improves search quality

- Optimize model serving for latency and GPU cost

- Turn customer and benchmark feedback into ranking improvements, with clear before/after numbers

Requirements 

You’re a great match if you:

- Are excited to help build Google for AI agents- and believe in Linkup’s mission 

- Have strong hands-on experience in information retrieval, ranking or search in production.

- Build rigorous evals and check the data behind every number

- Care about latency, cost and reliability as much as model quality

- Thrive in a fast-paced, high-ownership startup environment

Example Projects 

- Ship a new ranking model to production and prove the gain on our eval sets

- Push our models to the next level: better answers, lower latency, lower cost per query

- Build and maintain the evaluations framework that measures every change to our search engine

Our Stack 

Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face, vLLM, Ray, Spark / Databricks, Vespa, Kubernetes, GitHub Actions, Terraform

Details 

The ideal candidate will play a central role in our engineering team, partnering closely with the founders. The models you ship will decide what thousands of AI products read every day.

We offer a flexible remote‑work policy- see the details here .

Join us and leverage your expertise to push the boundaries of AI!

About Linkup 

Our Vision 

We believe in a future of AI agents and the agentic web . These digital entities can create more value for humanity than we ever could alone, but they depend on the internet to operate, collaborate, take action, and gather information.

AI agents need web search . To perform well, they require information that is current, reliable, and context‑specific—not the diffuse, steadily aging knowledge frozen at their last training cut‑off.

Modern web search is built for humans, not AIs . Instead of trusted facts, it serves links, ads, and click‑bait. People want visually engaging pages; AI systems need structured truth. An AI can absorb oceans of data, while human attention barely skims the surface. Humans think visually and intuitively; AI reasons in latent space.

Web 2.0 is sunsetting . The deck is being reshuffled, and the Bing‑Google search oligopoly is crumbling. Indexing ever more pages is no longer the goal; semantically organizing facts for AI systems is. In the coming agentic web, Google’s ad‑driven model has no natural home.

Search for AI must be rebuilt from the ground up . We are reconstructing the web as a rigorously structured knowledge layer, mapping every concept, entity, and claim into a coherent semantic graph. This foundation delivers verified facts and rich context to AI instantly, unlocking faster reasoning, higher accuracy, and radically more useful answers for everyone.

Humans search Google; AI searches Linkup. 

Our Mission 

Reality never stands still, and neither should intelligence. Linkup reconnects language models to a living stream of verified facts, ensuring AIs remain as current and insightful as the world they serve.

Our mission is to deliver the world’s freshest, most trusted knowledge to AIs.

Our Culture 

Our culture is built on the following values:

- Mission . We believe we play a critical role in building the agentic web. We are 100% committed to our mission of bringing the reality of the world to AI agents.

- Speed . We build fast, we build to last. We get things done, well.

- Ownership . We empower every team member to take ownership of their projects, ensuring they see them through to successful completion.

- Teamwork . Our strength lies in our unity. We rely on one another and embrace our diversity as a core asset.

- Humility . We maintain low egos, showing respect for others and continuously learning from their insights and experiences.

We expect all team member to take an active role in shaping our company culture.

Our Team 

We are a small technical team, working shoulder to shoulder to build the web of agents.

A bit more about our 3 co-founders:

- Philippe Mizrahi- Led the development of Lyft’s Autonomous Vehicles marketplace. Previously launched Amundsen , an open source search engine.

- Denis Charrier - Founding Engineer at Niland, an audio search company (acquired by Spotify), then Staff Engineer at Spotify. 15y of software development experience.

- Boris Toledano - Led robotics at Carrefour, after 3y at McKinsey & Co working on public affairs and digital transformation.

description:
ScorePlay is the AI-powered media infrastructure for sports, built to automate the content operations behind the world's biggest sports organizations. We work with 300+ leagues, competitions, teams and broadcasters – including Ligue 1 and Premier League clubs, NBA and NFL teams, the Tour de France, the Australian Open, and leading bodies like UEFA and FIBA – helping them turn every moment on and off the field into high-value, structured content . Founded in 2021 , we’re a 50-person team based between New York and Paris , growing 2x year over year with 98% retention. We’ve raised $20M+ from top investors including Alexis Ohanian and Harry Stebbing’s 20VC and elite athletes like Kevin Durant, Raphaël Varane, Mario Götze, Nico Rosberg and Giannis Antetokounmpo.

If you’re passionate about sports and thrive in fast-paced environments - and you want to help shape how the next generation of fans experience sports, you’re in the right place. We’re on track to become the global leader in sports media , and this is definitely the best time to join our adventure . 

About the Role

As our Head of People , you’ll own everything related to our growing workforce (65 people today). Compensation, leveling, performance, org design: most of it exists today and yours, and it’s yours to upgrade to make sure it remains best-in-class as we scale. You’ll lead a lean team across Talent Acquisition and Talent Development (2 people for now), work directly with the CEO and Head of Ops, and have a real say in how ScorePlay scales internationally.

It’s also a rare chance to answer a question most People leaders are only starting to ask: what does a high-performing company look like when AI changes roles, team sizes and what we hire for?

This is a hands-on builder role. You’ll design the frameworks yourself, make decisions with data and ship them.

Key Responsibilities 

- Organizational design & workforce planning: Design organizational structure, spans, team composition, and headcount plans as we scale, including how AI changes roles, team sizes, and what we hire for.

- Performance, leveling & talent management: Build consistent leveling and performance frameworks across functions. Oversee performance cycles and calibration, and own talent reviews, succession planning, and the resolution of legacy leveling inconsistencies.

- Compensation, equity & benefits: Build competitive, internally consistent compensation bands, equity frameworks, and regional benefits. Own compensation benchmarking, offer governance, and compensation cost discipline, with particular attention to US-market competitiveness.

- Hiring strategy & talent standards: Define hiring priorities, workforce needs, and senior hiring, and set a consistently high talent bar, including AI fluency.

- High-performer retention & growth: Identify and retain top talent, build meaningful career paths, and own succession and development plans. Monitor regretted attrition and address systemic retention risks.

- Manager effectiveness: Equip managers to hire, develop, evaluate, and retain strong teams. Set practical management standards and oversee manager development, with clear accountability for performance and people decisions.

- Culture & organizational health: Maintain a cohesive, high-performance culture across regions and hybrid teams. Identify and address organizational friction, engagement risks, and gaps in accountability or collaboration.

- People analytics & governance: Define clear People KPIs, review cadence, and decision frameworks. Lead strategic employment-structure decisions, including entity/EOR considerations, in partnership with Finance and Legal.

- People function leadership: Lead and develop the People team, ensuring strong execution of recruiting, employee lifecycle, employee relations, compliance, and HR operations through the team and appropriate external experts.

Qualifications 

- Experience building People programs in high-growth tech companies , ideally with 8+ years of progressive experience across People Operations, People Strategy, HRBP, or related roles.

- Proven ability to design and implement People frameworks , in at least two of the following areas: compensation and job leveling, performance management and calibration, talent development, or organizational design.

- Strong analytical and business judgment , with the ability to use data to diagnose organizational problems, evaluate trade-offs, and develop practical recommendations that balance employee experience, performance, and financial discipline.

- A first managerial experience required , having led and developed at least a small People or HR team.

- Comfort operating hands-on in a lean, fast-moving organization , building practical first versions of processes and systems rather than relying on large teams or extensive external support.

title: Forward Software Engineer
description:
About Mistral 

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms.

We are a dynamic, collaborative team passionate about AI and its potential to transform society. Our diverse workforce thrives in competitive environments and is committed to driving innovation. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

About The Job 

As a Forward Software Engineer, you will build the systems behind some of the hardest problems Mistral takes on.

You join our team of engineers in Applied AI. We gravitate towards hard problems, decide how to solve them, and ship fast. You work closely with our customer-facing teams, and what works goes into production with our customers and across the company. When a project needs it, you work directly on customer engagements.

We're looking for a strong software engineer who has shipped agentic or GenAI systems to production. You've felt the pain of agents that work in the demo and fall apart on real tasks: tool calls that fail silently, loops that never end, and quality that drifts after launch. That production depth is your edge. You build across the stack, and you'd rather ship a plain UI on a solid foundation than a polished UI on a fragile one.

You think like a founder. You start from the customer's problem, not the technology. You measure success by the value you deliver, and you care about building experiences people love to use. You like working at the edge of what AI can do today, and you push past it.

Your scope is end to end, from first prototype to production. You help set the standard for how the team builds agents that are reliable, observable, and safe to run against sensitive systems.

Security is a big part of where we're heading. If you're drawn to it, that's a strong plus. You might come from security with a real interest in AI engineering, or from AI engineering with a real interest in security. Both paths fit. Curiosity about how systems break, and a habit of learning fast from the people who know the domain, matter. Experience at a security company counts too.

What you will do 

- Build AI systems end to end, from first prototype to production.

- Design the agent architecture: orchestration, tool use, memory, retrieval, and the interfaces between agents and the systems they act on.

- Build across the stack, from backend services and APIs to the interfaces people use to work with agents.

- Turn what works for one customer into patterns and platforms that work across many, without rebuilding each time.

- Make systems hold up under real load: throughput, latency, cost, and failure recovery are part of the design from the start.

- Build security into agents from day one: permissions, sandboxing, prompt-injection defenses, and audit trails for agents that touch sensitive systems.

- Build the evaluation loop: task-level evals, tracing, and checks that catch agent failures and quality drift before customers do.

- Work with researchers, engineers, and customer-facing teams to turn hard problems into systems people rely on.

What We're Looking For 

- You have 5+ years building production software, with at least one agentic or GenAI system shipped to production that you ran after launch.

- You have full ability to ship across the stack: proficient NodeJS e.g. NextJS/Express/Fastify or similar or Python e.g. FastAPI. You are confident with TypeScript + React/NextJS or similar. Solid beats polished.

- You have hands-on depth in agent design: orchestration, tool use, retrieval, evaluation, and the ways agents fail in the real world.

- You work autonomously: you find the problem, decide the approach, and own the outcome.

- You communicate clearly with technical and non-technical audiences, and are fluent in English.

- You ship in increments and are obsessed with time to value

- You have product judgment: you learn what users need through customer-facing teams, cut scope hard, and care how the result feels to use.

Ideally you have 

- Open-source contributions, particularly in agents or LLMs.

- Experience deploying and running what you build: Docker, Kubernetes, Terraform, and AWS, GCP, or Azure.

- A security background in application, cloud, or AI security, such as prompt injection, securing agents, or supply chain (SBOM, SLSA). If that's you, flag it in your application.

- Experience building for security workflows, such as alert triage, threat hunting, or investigation agents, or with SIEM, XDR, or SOAR tooling.

How We Work in Applied AI 

- We care about people and outputs.

- What matters is what you ship, not the time you spend on it

- Bureaucracy is where urgency goes to vanish. You talk to whoever you need to talk to. The best idea wins, whether it comes from a principal engineer or someone in their first week.

- Always ask why. The best solutions come from deep understanding, not from copying what worked before

- We say what we mean. Feedback is direct, timely, and given because we care.

- No politics. Low ego, high standards.

- We embrace an unstructured environment and find joy in it.

What We Offer 

We offer a comprehensive benefits package designed to support your well-being, growth, and work-life balance. Benefits vary by country and may include healthcare coverage, parental leave, retirement plans, relocation support, wellness programs, meal and transportation allowances, and other location-specific perks.

For the most up-to-date details on benefits available in your location, please refer to our Benefits page .

description:
Présentation de Télécom SudParis :

Télécom SudParis est une grande école publique d'ingénieurs reconnue au meilleur niveau des sciences et technologies du numérique. La qualité de ses formations est basée sur l’excellence scientifique de son corps professoral et une pédagogie mettant l’accent sur les projets d’équipes, l’innovation de rupture et l’entreprenariat. Télécom SudParis fait partie de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, premier groupe d’école d’ingénieurs en France, et partage son campus avec Institut Mines-Télécom Business School. Télécom SudParis est co- fondatrice de l'Institut Polytechnique de Paris (IP Paris), Institut de Sciences et Technologies à vocation mondiale avec l’École polytechnique, l’ENSTA Paris, l’ENSAE Paris, l'ENPC et Télécom Paris. Vidéo présentation de Télécom SudParis 

À propos de l'Institut Mines-Télécom :

L'Institut Mines-Télécom (IMT) est un établissement public dédié à l'enseignement supérieur et la recherche pour l'innovation dans les domaines de l'ingénierie et du numérique. À l’écoute permanente du monde économique, l'IMT conjugue une forte légitimité académique et scientifique, une proximité avec les entreprises et un positionnement unique sur les transformations majeures au XXIe siècle : numériques, énergétiques, industrielles et éducatives siècle. Ses activités se déploient au sein des grandes écoles Mines et Télécom sous tutelle du ministre en charge de l’Industrie et des communications électroniques, de deux filiales et de partenaires associés ou sous convention. L'IMT est membre fondateur de l’Alliance Industrie du Futur. Il est doublement labellisé Carnot pour la qualité de sa recherche partenariale. Vidéo de présentation de l'Institut Mines-Télécom 

Missions

- Assurer des missions de recherche en théorie de l’information quantique, avec un accent particulier sur les systèmes quantiques bosoniques 

- Assurer des missions d’encadrement et de tutorat des étudiants 

- Contribuer à la notoriété de Télécom SudParis, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris 

Activités 

- Assurer des activités de recherche en théorie de l’information quantique 

- Étudier les propriétés mathématiques et informationnelles des états et canaux quantiques bosoniques, en mettant particulièrement l’accent sur les systèmes non gaussiens.

- Étudier et chercher à démontrer des inégalités entropiques quantiques intervenant en théorie de l’information quantique bosonique, notamment des inégalités liées à l’action des diviseurs de faisceau et d’autres transformations bosoniques physiquement pertinentes.

- Développer de nouveaux outils mathématiques pour l’analyse des états et canaux bosoniques non gaussiens, en s’appuyant notamment sur des méthodes issues de la théorie de l’information quantique, de l’analyse matricielle et des opérateurs, de la théorie de la majorisation et de domaines connexes.

- Appliquer ces résultats à la caractérisation de la transmission de l’information à travers les canaux quantiques bosoniques, en particulier à l’établissement de formules de capacité ainsi que de bornes supérieures ou inférieures sur les capacités de communication.

- Explorer les liens entre les méthodes développées et d’autres problématiques de la théorie de l’information quantique et de la physique mathématique.

- Contribuer à la réalisation des objectifs scientifiques et des livrables du projet de recherche.

- Présenter et discuter les résultats de recherche au sein de l’équipe ainsi qu’avec des collaborateurs extérieurs.

- Préparer des publications scientifiques présentant les résultats des travaux de recherche.

2. Assurer des activités d’enseignement, d’encadrement et de tutorat 

- Assurer des séances de travaux dirigés dans le cadre d’un cours de théorie de l’information quantique.

- Préparer et mettre à jour des feuilles d’exercices, des corrigés et d’autres supports pédagogiques pour ce cours.

- Encadrer des projets étudiants et, le cas échéant, des stages de recherche.

- Contribuer à l’accompagnement scientifique de doctorants et d’autres jeunes chercheurs travaillant sur des thématiques connexes.

3. Contribuer à la notoriété de Télécom SudParis, de l’Institut Mines-Télécom et de l’Institut Polytechnique de Paris 

- Publier les résultats des travaux de recherche dans des revues internationales à comité de lecture et dans des actes de conférences.

- Présenter les résultats de recherche lors de conférences internationales, d’ateliers, de séminaires et de rencontres scientifiques.

- Participer à des collaborations scientifiques avec des institutions académiques et des centres de recherche en France et à l’étranger.

- Contribuer à l’animation scientifique et à la visibilité du département et de l’établissement.

4. Activités diverses 

- Participer aux activités scientifiques et académiques du département et de l’établissement.

- Participer aux séminaires de recherche, aux réunions de projet et aux autres activités scientifiques collectives.

- Rendre compte de l’avancement et des résultats des activités de recherche dont il ou elle a la charge.

Formation

- Doctorat en physique, mathématiques, informatique, ingénierie, ou dans un domaine connexe pertinent pour la théorie de l’information quantique

- Expérience de recherche en théorie de l’information quantique, physique mathématique, théorie de la communication quantique, optique quantique théorique, ou dans un domaine étroitement lié

- Expérience des approches analytiques et mathématiques appliquées à des problèmes de théorie de l’information quantique.

Compétences, connaissances et expériences indispensables 

- Maîtrise de l’anglais écrit et oral.

- Connaissance de la mécanique quantique et de la théorie de l’information quantique.

- Connaissance des canaux quantiques, des entropies quantiques et des méthodes issues de la théorie de l’information.

- Capacité à formuler et à traiter de manière autonome des problèmes théoriques complexes.

title: CENTRALE LYON - Post Doctoral Open and Flexible System-Level Evaluation Framework for Emerging AI Computing Architectures
description:
Emerging computing technologies – non-volatile and ferroelectric memories, analog and digital in-memory computing, silicon photonics, 3D integration, and heterogeneous chiplets – offer major gains in energy efficiency, latency, bandwidth, and functionality. Their potential cannot, however, be established from device or circuit results alone: it requires a rigorous link between technology characteristics, architectural choices, workload mapping, and application-level figures of merit. 

The Electronics group at the Lyon Institute of Nanotechnology (INL) is seeking a (m/f) postdoctoral researcher to develop an open, modular and extensible system-level evaluation framework for design space exploration (DSE) and system-design-technology co-optimization (SDTCO) of emerging computing architectures. The focus is at the interface of computer architecture, accelerator design, performance modelling and hardware-software codesign, while making systematic use of lower-level device, circuit and array results so that architectural conclusions remain physically credible. 

The objective is to convert low-level results – compact models, measured or simulated KPIs, variability and reliability constraints, and multi-objective Pareto fronts – into parameterized architectural models supporting efficient exploration of accelerators for emerging AI workloads. The framework must enable both bottom-up projection, from device/circuit/array choices toward system performance, and top-down constraint propagation, from targets for energy, latency, throughput, accuracy, robustness and area toward technology and circuit requirements. It will consolidate ongoing INL activities in predictive system assessment, DTCO, emerging memories, compute-in-memory and photonic computing, integrating or extending existing components with emphasis on openness, reproducibility and reusability. 

A core scientific challenge is to represent cross-layer trade-offs without hiding their origin: rather than isolated energy or latency numbers, the framework should expose bottlenecks, sensitivities, feasibility limits, break-even points and opportunities and identify the regimes in which a technology becomes advantageous. Target workloads span edge inference through to transformer-inspired models, with use cases in vision, audio and sensor processing, sparse and vector/matrix operations, and on-device learning. 

Expected outcomes: a maintainable evaluation environment combining fast exploration with selected higherfidelity validation paths; cross-layer models and interface contracts, reusable data schemes, benchmarking flows, system-level Pareto analyses and design guidelines for emerging AI accelerators – a decision-support instrument for future research projects.

Candidate profile: PhD in Electrical or Electronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science or a related discipline, with a strong background in several of: computer architecture and AI accelerators; performance, energy and area modelling; design space exploration and multi-objective optimization; hardwaresoftware co-design and workload mapping; emerging memories, compute-in-memory or photonic computing. Strong Python skills and sound software-engineering practice are essential; experience with SystemC, C/C++, RISCV simulation, QEMU, PyTorch/ONNX workload flows, architecture simulators (NeuroSim, CiMLoop/AccelForge, Timeloop or similar) will be appreciated. Familiarity with circuit-level modelling or EDA is an asset, but the focus is architectural and system-level research. 

Environment: the position is hosted by the Electronics group at INL (UMR CNRS 5270), Ecole Centrale de Lyon, Écully, France – an interdisciplinary environment spanning devices, circuits, architectures, design automation, photonics and integrated systems, with national and European collaborations. 

Starting date: Fall 2026

title: Chief of Staff Intern
description:
What is Finary?

Money is broken. Most people's wealth sits in products they did not choose, with fees they cannot see, and a private banker costs more than they will ever pay. We are putting one in everyone's pocket: the same quality of advice for a €10K saver and a €10M client.

Mounir launched Finary in 2021, and more than 1M people now track their wealth with us, for free. Finary AI turns that financial context into a plan, and our own investment products and in-house wealth advisors (Finary One) make it real: clarity on what you have, guidance on where you are going, action to get there.

Why now?

AI makes this vision possible, and 3 things make it hard to copy:

- Data: years of per-user financial history, goals and risk profiles that no public dataset holds.

- Brand: half of our new users come from our own channels, and 1 signup in 5 names our YouTube channel.

- Licences: stocks, ETFs and crypto on one regulated platform, passportable across Europe. We started early, when a simple registration was enough: PSAN in 2022, Investment Firm licence in March 2026, MiCA in July 2026. Since July, every crypto platform in Europe must be licensed or stop.

Many fintechs will have the AI, and a few will have the licences. We have all 3. We raised €40M from Hedosophia, Y Combinator and Speedinvest, alongside founders and operators like Steve Anavi & Alexandre Prot (Qonto), Matthieu Rouif (Photoroom), Eric Demuth (Bitpanda), Axel Weber (former UBS Chairman) and Harsh Sinha (CTO at Wise). There's never been a more exciting time to join.

What we offer 

We're 70 builders who genuinely love what they do: real ownership from day one, tier-1 salary and equity, offices in the heart of Paris with hybrid remote, and quarterly gatherings we actually look forward to.

We hire A-players who are as kind as they are demanding, people whose ideas transform not just our product but the way we work and think. Our culture is direct, transparent, and built on radical candor: we challenge each other openly, then commit. And we don't hedge on AI. It's the single most important skill of the next decade and a real bar here. Everyone at Finary has rebuilt how they work around it. If that's already second nature to you, you'll be surrounded by people pushing that frontier every day.

Read more about our values here .

The role

The CEO Office owns Finary's most important strategic projects, the delivery of the business plan, company’s operating rituals and runs the board and investor relations. Today one Chief of Staff carries all of it. You join as a real partner: you own a share of these projects from day one and move key topics forward fast, side by side with the Chief of Staff and the CEO.

What you will do

- Take one area of the company and measurably improve its metrics.

- Lead the analyses behind big decisions: business plan updates, international expansion, new offers and segments. You turn a question into a recommendation the leadership team can act on.

- Run the board operating rhythm and the monthly reporting, with numbers you have checked yourself.

- Work with Finance on budget, targets, forecast and costs.

- Own Finary's operating rituals (weekly kick-off, all-hands, performance reviews, leadership topics) and make them sharper.

What success looks like

- After 1 month: you know Finary's business, numbers and new vision, and you run the operating rituals.

- After 3 months: you co-run the board and the monthly reporting, and the team you focus on performs measurably better.

- After 6 months: you are a multiplier across teams. The CEO Office delivers more, faster.

Who you are

- You have a track record of winning: a competition, a sport, a project where you went further than anyone expected.

- You own outcomes, not tasks. You come back with proposals, not questions.

- You are extremely rigorous with numbers: models, Excel, data. Nothing leaves your hands unchecked.

- You write short, clear English that a board member reads in 5 minutes.

- You are an AI pioneer.

- You build trust fast and get things done through people, without authority.

- You are discreet and put the company first.

- You are in your final year or a recent graduate of a top business or engineering school, fluent in French and English.

Bonus: a first internship in strategy consulting, ideally followed by startup ops or product. Being a Finary user.

Practical details

title: Senior Mechanical Engineer
description:
Join the Wingtra team and become part of this venture-backed robotics scaleup with a global and international team of 125+ dedicated Wingtranauts who want to see their actions have a positive and lasting impact on the world. Founded more than 8 years ago at ETH Zurich, Europe’s leading robotics university, our goal is to build the best aerial robots to digitize the world at the push of a button and set the basis for faster and better decisions. Wingtra provides efficient and reliable data solutions to a variety of industries ranging from mining, construction and agriculture to humanitarian organizations, environmentalists and wildlife monitoring groups. 

We are reaching for the stars and together we might just get there. Open communication, asking hard questions and valuing diverse viewpoints are but a few things that will help us achieve our goals. Above all we will never stop learning and striving to help each other reach our maximum potential.

Help us take Wingtra’s new product platforms from fast prototypes to reliable series production. Embedded in the engineering team, you own mechanical design, qualification and industrialization through initial ramp-up. Together we deliver a qualified product, a complete product file and a working production line. We are early adopters of AI and actively build agentic workflows across engineering, from design and test planning to execution and analysis.

Responsibilities 

- 
Take a new aircraft from concept to series production. You work in a small team with electronics designers and test engineers. You get direct feedback from prototypes, flight tests and production builds.

- 
Design and iterate lightweight parts. You design, build and test parts and assemblies, then improve them until they are ready for production.

- 
Choose materials and processes with care. You balance performance, volumes, unit cost, tooling investment and lead times.

- 
Own DFX. You design for manufacturing, assembly, quality, cost and serviceability, and you settle tolerances, interfaces and process constraints early.

- 
Work hand in hand with suppliers. You partner with sourcing on technical feasibility, tooling and part iterations.

- 
Own qualification. You qualify parts with the intended production materials and processes, and you agree product-specific acceptance criteria with the test engineers.

- 
Deliver the production-ready product file. CAD, 2D drawings, tolerances, BOMs, material and process specifications and acceptance criteria.

- 
Hand over a running line. Once the qualification gates have passed and ramp-up is complete, you hand the line and the product file to Production and Production Engineering.

Requirements 

- 
You have several years of experience taking mechanical products through the full lifecycle: prototype, series production and quality monitoring at the customer. Ideally on structurally critical products at volumes of hundreds to a few thousand units.

- 
You are strong in CAD (Solidworks/PDM preferred), tolerance analysis and material selection.

- 
You have practical experience with injection molding as well as additive manufacturing for functional plastic parts.

- 
You prototype fast and pragmatically, then qualify and document with discipline.

- 
You like hands-on work: builds, testing and working with suppliers.

- 
You use AI for design exploration, qualification planning and data analysis. You check its output, share new workflows and keep raising the team’s bar.

- 
You are curious, flexible and collaborative, with a real drive to build the next great thing.

If you enjoy teamwork more than being the individual superhero, and if you thrive in a feedback-driven culture and an exciting, unconventional yet structured and progressive start-up environment, we would love to hear from you.

title: Sales Manager CH, KI-Software für Psychotherapeut:innen
description:
Über VIA HealthTech

VIA macht aus einer Therapiesitzung ein fertiges Sitzungsprotokoll und aus Sitzungsprotokollen vollständige psychologische Berichte. Arbeit, die Therapeut:innen bisher mehrere Stunden pro Woche gekostet hat.

Wir sind die marktführende KI-Assistenz für Psychotherapeut:innen. Über 4.000 Psychotherapeut:innen im DACH-Raum nutzen VIA, wir verarbeiten Hunderttausende Sitzungen pro Monat. Wir sind nach ISO 27001:2022 zertifiziert und verfügen über ein BSI-C5-Testat.

Wir sind ein multidisziplinäres Team in Berlin-Mitte. Marktführer in Deutschland zu sein, ist erst der Startpunkt. Die Schweiz ist unser nächster Markt, und du baust ihn mit auf.

Die Rolle

Du bist unsere erste Person im Schweizer Markt. Du baust die Pipeline von Grund auf, entwickelst das Playbook und führst es selbst aus.

In Deutschland läuft unser Funnel vor allem über Webinare: Therapeut:innen melden sich an, testen VIA 14 Tage und buchen selbst. Du findest heraus, was davon in der Schweiz funktioniert und was anders laufen muss: Qualifizierung am Telefon, Cold-Calling, andere Outbound- und Inbound-Kanäle, Verbände, Weiterbildungsinstitute, grössere Organisationen als eigener Kanal. Du testest, misst und skalierst, wo der Hebel am grössten ist.

Du arbeitest eng mit Marketing an Zielgruppen, Kampagnen und Botschaften für den Schweizer Markt und gibst direkt zurück, was im Gespräch wirklich zieht.

Die Rolle ist senior gedacht. Wenn du mid-level, aber aussergewöhnlich schnell und hungrig bist, bewirb dich trotzdem.

Deine Aufgaben

- Den Markt öffnen. Du identifizierst die wichtigsten Zielgruppen in der Schweiz: selbstständige psychologische Psychotherapeut:innen, Psychiater:innen, Organisationen der psychologischen Psychotherapie, Ambulatorien und Kliniken. Du priorisierst, wo wir zuerst gewinnen.
- Leads in Kund:innen verwandeln. Qualifizierungsgespräche, Webinare, Demos, Follow-up während der Testphase, Abschluss. Du bist die zentrale Ansprechperson für Schweizer Kund:innen.
- Neue Kanäle erschliessen. Berufsverbände wie FSP, ASP und SBAP, Weiterbildungsinstitute, Fachveranstaltungen und Kongresse. Erstansprache per Telefon, E-Mail und LinkedIn, wo sie sich lohnt.
- Playbook bauen, während du verkaufst. Was konvertiert, welche Einwände in der Schweiz wirklich kommen (etwa zu Datenschutz und Datenhaltung), welche Sequenz funktioniert.
- Zahlen verantworten. Deine KPIs entlang des Funnels, gemeinsam mit unserem Commercial Engine Lead, der Tracking und Infrastruktur baut.
- Sales-Enablement-Material. Du passt an, was zum Verkaufen und Vermarkten in der Schweiz am besten wirkt, von Sprache bis Preisdarstellung in CHF.
- Feedback ins Produkt bringen. Was Schweizer Kund:innen brauchen und woran Deals scheitern, besprichst du direkt mit dem Produktteam.
Dein Profil

Must-have

- Nachgewiesene Abschlüsse im B2B-Vertrieb in der Schweiz, idealerweise SaaS oder Digital Health, belegbar in Zahlen
- Echte Hunter-Mentalität. Du hast bereits aktiv Erstkontakte am Telefon gemacht und hast damit kein Problem. Wenn dich 40 Gespräche am Tag abschrecken, ist das die falsche Rolle
- Kenntnis des Schweizer Gesundheitswesens oder die Fähigkeit, dich sehr schnell einzuarbeiten: Grundversicherung, Anordnungsmodell, Rolle von Kantonen und Verbänden
- Glaubwürdigkeit gegenüber Therapeut:innen. Psychotherapeut:innen vertrauen vor allem Psychotherapeut:innen. Entweder bringst du diesen Hintergrund mit, oder du arbeitest dich so schnell und so tief ein, dass man es dir im Gespräch nicht anmerkt
- Systemdenken. Du baust reproduzierbare Prozesse statt Einzelfälle, mit dem Ziel, dass dein Ansatz auch ohne dich funktioniert
- Hunger und unternehmerischer Ehrgeiz. Du willst einen neuen Markt aufbauen, nicht eine Quote abarbeiten
- Kommunikationsstärke mit Abschlussfokus. Empathisch und auf Augenhöhe, denn Psychotherapeut:innen merken sofort, wenn jemand verkauft, statt zu verstehen
- Selbstständige, strukturierte und datengetriebene Arbeitsweise, auch remote und ohne Team vor Ort, sowie sicherer Umgang mit CRM-Systemen
- Deutsch auf verhandlungssicherem Niveau (C2), auch Schweizerdeutsch, gutes Englisch
- Verfügbarkeit am frühen Abend. Unsere Zielgruppe ist häufig erst nach der letzten Sitzung erreichbar, Termine zwischen 17 und 19 Uhr gehören dazu. Im Gegenzug gestaltest du deinen Tag frei
Von Vorteil

- Französisch und/oder Italienisch, um später auch die weiteren Gebiete anzusprechen
- Ein bestehendes Netzwerk in der Schweizer Psychotherapie- oder Psychiatrieszene
- Erfahrung mit Funnels, in denen Marketing und Vertrieb ineinandergreifen: Performance-Marketing, Webinare, Trials, Self-Service
- Anerkennung als Psychotherapeut:in, psychologische Ausbildung oder mehrjährige Erfahrung im Gesundheitswesen
- Vertriebserfahrung mit Praxen, Heilberufen oder Spitälern in der Schweiz
- Hands-on-Erfahrung mit Sales-Automation, LinkedIn Sales Navigator oder Outbound-Tooling
- Erfahrung im Markteintritt oder Aufbau eines Vertriebs von 0 auf 1
Diese Rolle ist nichts für dich, wenn

- Du ein Team suchst, das für dich telefoniert.
- Du eine fertige Pipeline oder ein bestehendes Länderteam erwartest. Du baust beides.
- Du weder Hunger noch besonderen Ehrgeiz mitbringst. Wir sind ein ambitioniertes Team und stellen entsprechend ein.
Was wir bieten

- Einen Markt, den du prägst. Du bist die erste Person von VIA in der Schweiz. Was du aufbaust, wird zum Fundament unseres Schweizer Geschäfts
- Ein Team, das überperformt. DACH-Marktführer für KI-Assistenz in der Psychotherapie in zwei Jahren, bootstrapped. Unsere Pläne von hier sind deutlich grösser, und wir stellen Menschen ein, die das mitgestalten wollen
