description:
This role is open only to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations. 

If you've built something before, start here

The hardest part of a startup usually isn't the code. It's finding customers who really need what you build and getting them to change how they work. At Scalera, that part is done: manufacturers, suppliers and contractors across Switzerland, Austria and Germany already run their tenders through us every day.

What we need now are people who can take the next unsolved problem and turn it into a product customers can't do without. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first engineer somewhere, or built something people paid for, this role was written for you.

About Scalera

Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Large manufacturers and suppliers still run their most document-heavy processes by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate them one by one. Our product matching already handles 1,400 tender positions in 16 minutes at 98% precision, work that used to take a sales rep most of a day.

What you'll do

You'll be part product manager, part engineer. You'll spend real time with customers and help shape what we build. Sometimes you'll spot the next problem yourself, and sometimes we'll hand you a clear priority to run with.

- Spend real time with customers. Join calls and site visits, sit with the people who do the work, and understand why they do it the way they do. You'll know their problems firsthand, not from a ticket.

- Shape what to build. Turn what you hear into a clear problem, a scope and a plan, and push back when the obvious request isn't the real need. When we bring you a priority, you'll own how it gets solved.

- Build it. Design and build backend services in Go and Python that turn messy tenders, catalogs and purchase orders into data customers can rely on.

- Ship, then check. Get it in front of customers fast, watch how they actually use it, and iterate.

- Own it in production. When something breaks at a customer, it's yours to understand and fix.

- Build with AI. Use AI heavily in how you work, and design systems that agents can use as well as people.

What success looks like after 3 months

- There's a part of the product people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next

- You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version

- You've shipped features from both sources: priorities we set and ideas from your own customer conversations

- At least once, you've talked us out of building something customers didn't really need

- You've left a part of the platform simpler than you found it

You'll probably thrive here if

- You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a product line, or a side project with paying users

- You've built and run backend systems in production that other people depend on. We care more about your judgment than your language; you're strong in Go or Python and happy to work in both

- You're solid on data modeling, API design and messy real-world data

- You'd rather talk to a customer than wait for a spec

- You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is

- You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title

- Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going

- You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls

- You make things simpler over time, not more clever

- You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement

You probably won't enjoy it if

- You just want to code and go home

- You don't like talking to customers, whether on calls or on the occasional site visit

- Ambiguity and chaos bother you

- You want a well-defined backlog handed to you

- Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount

Our stack

Go and Python (FastAPI), PostgreSQL, GCP, and LLMs throughout the document pipeline. You don't need to know all of it on day one.

How we hire

- Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions.

- Technical deep-dive call : walk us through something you built from scratch, the decisions you made and what went wrong.

- Meet Scalera Day : join us remotely to work on a real problem with real (anonymized) construction documents, and meet the team.

- Offer : if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer.

Working at Scalera

- Remote within the EU or EEA 

- Small team, no bureaucracy. You'll work directly with the CEO, CTO, VP Engineering and Customer Success

- Competitive compensation

Founders and former founders: if you're unsure whether you fit, send a few lines about what you built and why you moved on. We read every one.

title: Senior AI/ML Engineer
description:
This role is also open to candidates living in the EU or EEA. We can't consider applications from other locations. 

If you've built something before, start here

Most ML jobs hand you a benchmark. This one hands you a business problem with paying customers and their real data. Construction tenders are long, messy and full of trade jargon, and every decision a customer makes on our platform becomes a labeled example you can train on.

We need someone who can turn that data into models that customers notice: from the first experiment to the model serving production traffic, and back again when a customer says it got something wrong. If you've founded a company (whether it worked out or not), been the first ML engineer somewhere, or shipped a model people paid for, this role was written for you.

About Scalera

Scalera is an ETH Zurich spin-off building AI for the €200B+ European construction industry. Manufacturers, wholesalers and suppliers in Switzerland, Austria and Germany still run their most document-heavy work by hand, from reading 300-page tenders to retyping purchase orders into their ERP. We automate that work one process at a time, and ML sits at the center of every one of them.

What you'll own

You'll own the ML behind our products, end to end. In practice that means:

- Training and fine-tuning : embedding models, rerankers, classifiers and LLMs, trained on our own data.

- Document understanding : models that pull structure, quantities and product specs out of tenders, orders and catalogs.

- Product matching : retrieval and LLM agents that match tender positions to the right products.

- Evaluation : offline benchmarks, per-customer evals and gates that keep a new model from shipping if it makes things worse.

- Training and serving infrastructure : automated retrain pipelines, GPU serving and vector search in production.

- Customer problems : when a model gets something wrong for a customer, finding out why and fixing it.

What success looks like after 3 months

- There's a model or part of the pipeline people now think of as yours, and you're the one deciding what happens to it next.

- You've spotted a problem nobody asked you to solve, made the case for it, and shipped a first version.

- A model you trained runs in production, and customers can see the difference in their results.

- Retraining runs automatically, and nothing reaches customers without passing an eval you designed.

- You've cut LLM cost or latency by replacing an expensive step with a smaller model of your own.

- You've decided at least one thing we should stop building.

You'll probably thrive here if

- You've taken something from zero to one: a company, a model in production, or a side project with real users.

- You've trained and fine-tuned models yourself, ideally embeddings, retrieval or document models, and evaluated them honestly on held-out data.

- You've built with LLMs in production and know where agents fail.

- You write strong Python and can run what you build: Docker, CI/CD, and cloud on GCP, AWS or Azure.

- You measure before you believe, and a single aggregate score doesn't convince you.

- You'd rather open a customer's actual document than wait for a spec.

- You're comfortable with ambiguity. You can make progress while the problem is still half-defined, which at a startup it usually is.

- You want a large scope of responsibility and are happy to own things well beyond your job title.

- Rapidly changing requirements don't throw you. When customers or priorities shift, you adapt and keep going.

- You enjoy direct customer contact and want to be on customer calls.

- You write clearly in English. German is a plus, not a requirement.

You probably won't enjoy it if

- You just want to code and go home.

- You don't like talking to customers.

- Ambiguity and chaos bother you.

- You want a well-defined research agenda handed to you.

- You'd rather hand a model to someone else to deploy and debug.

- Your main goal is managing people soon. Here, scope grows with what you own, not with headcount.

Our stack

Python and PyTorch, open-weight and frontier LLMs, LangGraph, Langfuse, PostgreSQL with pgvector, Pinecone, and GCP. You don't need to know all of it on day one.

How we hire

- Screening call (30 min) with our VP Engineering. It's two-way: ask us anything, including the hard questions.

- Technical deep-dive call : walk us through a model or system you built, the decisions you made and what went wrong in production.

- Meet Scalera Day : come to our office in Zürich, work on a real problem with real (anonymized) tender data, and meet the team.

- Offer : if it's a fit on both sides, we'll move quickly to an offer.

title: Chief Customer Officer
description:
Work from anywhere, impact everywhere 

Diversity is at the heart of who we are at Xapo Bank. 
We're a fully distributed team of over 160 Xapiens that work remotely from 50+ countries around the world.

Our beginning: A world that enjoys economic freedom and wealth protection,no matter where you live or who is running your country.
To achieve that, we search the world for the best people for the job. 
We work hard, think globally, and inspire each other to learn and grow. 
We are committed to changing the way things are done.

Although we are headquartered in Gibraltar, this is a full time, 100% remote position 
Work from anywhere! 

Position overview

Xapo's product suite has grown from a Bitcoin vault into a full member proposition: BTC and USD accounts that pay interest, a global card with Bitcoin cashback, Bitcoin-backed loans, a growing suite of BTC wealth and credit products, and access to stocks, ETFs, and stablecoins, all inside one regulated relationship. 

Xapo is a bank, and a bank earns on the money its members choose to hold with it. Each of those products shipped well. What hasn't yet existed is a single owner of the economics of the customer relationship: one person accountable for winning the right members, growing what they hold with us, and keeping them, and for the balance-sheet products that make that possible.

The Chief Customer Officer is a new role at the top of the house, reporting to the CEO. You will run the stream that grows what members hold with Xapo, and you will own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. It brings growth, client coverage, product management, and product design under one leader who is judged on customer contribution, the assets attracted and kept, and the members who stay. This is a customer-focused role in the most commercial sense: what a member earns from us, not the feature we shipped, is the centre of every decision.

The measure of success is a Customer P&L that grows on what members hold and keep: LTV:CAC improving, approved-to-paid rising, churn falling, and customer contribution the business can plan against.

This is a banking role, not a requirements-gathering role, a marketing role, or a role you can run from a dashboard. Products are priced on the balance sheet and judged on the money they attract and keep.

The mandate

- Own the Customer P&L, retail and institutional. 
You own customer contribution: customer gross profit from what members' balances earn, secured lending, Bitcoin yield, and conversion, stocks and ETFs, less the cost of winning and keeping members. We earn on what members hold, not on what they tap, send, or click, so you run on assets held and the margin they earn, not payment volume. Good looks like a Customer P&L the Exco and Board can plan against, where every line has a number you own and can explain, up or down.

- Grow what members hold with us, through earning products run like a banker would. 
You own the roadmap for the balance-sheet products: deposits and savings, lending and credit, and trading and structured. Each is led by a mission PM who is a banker, owning a product's contribution and its price on the balance sheet, not a backlog. Requirements go through the gate; the economics are the job. Every item is priced by Finance before it is built, on a shared risk appetite with Risk and Treasury. Good looks like products that scale assets held and member lifetime value at a risk profile the Board actually approved.

- Win the right members, efficiently. 
You own Growth: audience, lifecycle, and content, with one head accountable for the path from approval to paid. You own CAC and approved-to-paid, find the members who bring other members, and activate them in week one. Every incentive is priced before it runs. Good looks like net paid-member growth that improves every quarter, at a CAC that LTV comfortably justifies, because you diagnosed where the funnel leaks rather than spending more to fill it.

- Keep members, and deepen the relationship with the ones who hold balances. 
Retention is the most efficient growth we have. You own churn, and you own Client Coverage: relationship managers who sell the missions' products to the members who hold balances, and loop demand back into the roadmap. You are accountable for net new AUM flow, covered-book retention, and products per covered member, and for growth that is broad-based rather than concentrated in a few accounts. Good looks like falling churn and AUM growth from members who stay and expand rather than members re-acquired at cost.

- Make the value of Xapo visible, and the experience effortless. 
You own Product Design: one design system and one shell, so that members see the value of what they are earning clearly and early, and find every task simple. You design the proposition in the stream with Finance and partner with Operations, who run onboarding, KYC, support, cards, and payments, to remove friction at the points that affect members most. Good looks like members who understand their return, complete what they set out to do, and stay.

- Build one Customer organisation, not four. 
Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design come together under one operating model: one set of key results read weekly from one source, shared frameworks for discovery and prioritisation, and real career paths for the people in it. Engineering is pulled to a single ranked roadmap, and nobody in your line has engineers of their own. Good looks like fewer hand-offs per outcome and a number for every cell that its owner explains every week.

- Bring the regulated-bank and crypto-native lens to every customer call. 
You understand that a KYC onboarding decision and an AML monitoring decision carry different risk appetites, that a false positive at the gate is a paid-for member lost, and that a proposition built for a crypto-native power user can still fail a first-time bank customer. You can sit in the same room as a CRO, an MLRO, a CFO, and an engineering lead and make a customer case that survives all four conversations.

How you'll operate

This part matters as much as the mandate. The known failure mode for this role, in any company, is a CCO with a polished customer-insight deck and no ownership of the number. That is disqualifying here.

- You lead from inside the work. You sit in on growth reviews, mission PM reviews, client meetings, and member calls, not just steering committees. PMs, designers, and relationship managers three levels down know your name because you've solved problems with them.

- You move people with the business case, not the whip. When a priority needs to change, you diagnose the problem, build the case with data and the economics, and show teams why it matters, so they re-prioritise because they're convinced, not because they were told. Your authority comes from being right and being useful, not from your title.

- You have extreme ownership. You own the Customer P&L and the member metrics beneath it, not the feature ship date. If a launch didn't move contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, or churn, you don't report "the roadmap item shipped", you change the approach.

- You have genuine gravitas. Senior, experienced leaders welcome your input because you've earned the standing to give it. You can challenge any executive's plan, including the CEO's, constructively, with evidence, and be thanked for it, because your challenge makes their work stronger.

- You diagnose before you prescribe. You can walk into a leaking funnel, a churning segment, or a product that isn't earning and find the structural cause, then fix the economics, not just the symptom.

What you'll have done 

- 10+ years in senior commercial or customer leadership (CCO, Chief Growth or Commercial Officer, MD or Head of Retail or Wealth, or equivalent) in digital banking, fintech, or payments, including meaningful time in a regulated environment (banking licence, e-money, or equivalent prudential/conduct regime).

- Crypto-native credibility: hands-on experience building and growing customer propositions on or around digital assets, custody, on-chain flows, Bitcoin-backed lending, or similar. You don't need Bitcoin explained to you, and you don't need banking explained to you either.

- Customer P&L ownership: you have owned a customer or product P&L judged on contribution, balances, and margin rather than transaction volume, and you are fluent in NIM, unit economics, customer contribution, and LTV:CAC.

- Growth and lifecycle: a track record of acquiring, activating, and retaining members in a regulated, KYC-heavy environment, improving approved-to-paid and churn while holding CAC to a level that LTV justifies, not just growth-hacking a free consumer app.

- Banking-grade product leadership: you have led product management for balance-sheet products such as savings, lending, or structured products, priced with Finance, with PMs who own a product's economics rather than a backlog. Experience with client coverage or relationship-managed models for high-balance and institutional clients is a strong advantage.

- Commercial and risk fluency: you can build a customer business case that survives scrutiny from Finance, Risk, and Compliance in the same meeting, and you know the difference between growth that's sustainable and growth that's borrowed from tomorrow's risk appetite.

- A track record of outcomes you can narrate: specific LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, AUM, or contribution numbers you owned, bets you killed when the data didn't support them, and outcomes you can prove.

The first 90 days

Day 30: The Customer P&L baseline is documented across retail and institutional: customer contribution, LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, net paid-member growth, and assets attracted and kept. You have formed your own independent view of where members are won, lost, and under-served, and shared it with the CEO and Board. 
Day 60: The unified Customer operating model is live: one set of key results across Growth, Client Coverage, Mission PMs, and Product Design, read weekly from one source. Every mission PM owns a product's contribution and its price, and the roadmap is ranked on what it earns, built with Finance and the line leads. 
Day 90: At least one measurable improvement in LTV:CAC, approved-to-paid, churn, or net new AUM flow is live and attributable to a change you made, not a feature ship, an outcome moved. Every cell in your line has defined key results and an owner who explains the number every week.

What this role is not

- Not a requirements-gathering role. Mission PMs are bankers who own a product's contribution and price, not a backlog. You partner with Technology, Finance, and Operations on execution; you don't run those functions.

- Not a volume role. If your primary output is card spend, transfer volume, or a shipped list rather than assets held and the margin they earn, we have both failed.

- Not a reporting layer. If your primary output is a customer-insight deck or a roadmap deck, we have both failed.

- Not a role that can be done from a distance. Remote-first means distributed, not detached.

Other requirements

- A dedicated workspace.

- A reliable internet connection with the fastest speed possible in your area.

- Alignment with Our Values and the Xapo Values-Driven Leadership principles.

Why work for Xapo?

Impact Globally, Work Remotely.

- 
Shape the Future 
Improve lives through cutting-edge technology, work 100% remotely from anywhere in the world.

- 
Great work-life balance
Build amazing things with a balance of autonomy and collaborative teamwork. Set your own work schedule and make use of a flexible PTO plan when you need to recharge. 

- 
Expect Excellence
Collaborate, learn, and grow with a high-performance team. Learn how you learn best - from books to conferences, you'll get a yearly budget for your individual learning and development goals.

description:
Würenlos (AG) · 100 % · ca. 50 % bei Kunden vor Ort 

Bei der AKSA Würenlos AG entwickeln, realisieren und betreuen wir hochverfügbare Notstromlösungen – individuell, technisch anspruchsvoll und geschäftskritisch für unsere Kunden.

Unsere Steuerungstechniker:innen für Projekte begleiten eine Anlage bis zur Abnahme. Danach übernimmst Du: Du verantwortest die Steuerungstechnik unserer Anlagen im Betrieb – bei Retrofit-Projekten, Änderungen und im Service. Dafür brauchst Du dasselbe Können wie im Projektgeschäft, nur setzt Du es an bestehenden Anlagen ein, die oft anders aussehen als auf dem Plan.

Wenn Du nicht einfach Störungen beheben, sondern Ursachen verstehen, Lösungen konzipieren und Verantwortung übernehmen möchtest, bist Du bei uns richtig.

Deine Aufgaben 

Elektrokonstruktion 

- Erstellung komplexer Stromlaufpläne für Retrofit-Projekte und Anlagenänderungen (eXs-CAD) gemäss Konzept

- Aufnahme und Nachführung bestehender Schemas, auch bei Fremdfabrikaten und lückenhafter Dokumentation

Automationsplanung 

- Verantwortung für Steuerungslösungen in Retrofit- und Service-Projekten

- Unterstützung bei der Erarbeitung von Retrofit-Konzepten inkl. Umschaltplan und Rückfallebene, abgestimmt mit dem Projektleiter

- Integration von Notstromanlagen in übergeordnete Systeme (SPS, Leitsysteme, Gebäudeautomation)

Steuerungssysteme 

- Programmierung und Anpassung von SPS-Programmen, auch in fremden und älteren Systemen

- Parametrierung und Optimierung von Generatorsteuerungen (z. B. ComAp, Cummins PCC)

- Anpassung und Optimierung von Netzersatz-, Synchronisations- und Lastmanagementfunktionen

Service, Tests und Inbetriebnahme 

- Analyse umfassender Störungen vor Ort und Ableitung nachhaltiger Lösungen

- Test von Änderungen im Prüffeld und Inbetriebnahme nach Retrofits und Anlagenänderungen beim Kunden

- Durchführung anspruchsvoller Prüfungen der Steuerungs- und Elektrotechnik

Dokumentation und Standards 

- Sicherstellung einer sauberen, nachvollziehbaren Dokumentation aller Änderungen

- Rückmeldung von Erfahrungen aus dem Feld ans Engineering zur Weiterentwicklung von Standards

Team und Zusammenarbeit 

- Übernahme der Anlagen von den Projekt-Steuerungstechniker:innen nach der Abnahme

- Fachliche Unterstützung der Servicetechniker:innen bei steuerungstechnischen Fragen

- Technische Ansprechperson für Kunden, Betreiber und Projektleitende im After-Sales

Dein Profil 

- Abgeschlossene Ausbildung im Bereich Elektrotechnik, Automation oder vergleichbar

- Weiterbildung (z.B. HF Systemtechnik oder ähnlich) von Vorteil

- Erfahrung in der Steuerungstechnik im industriellen Umfeld

- Fundierte Erfahrung in Inbetriebnahme, Fehlersuche und im Umgang mit komplexen Anlagen

- Erfahrung im Schema-Engineering (vorzugsweise eXs) – Du erstellst Schemas, nicht nur Änderungen

- Erfahrung mit SPS-Systemen

- Erfahrung mit Umbauten oder Modernisierungen bestehender Anlagen

- Erfahrung mit Generatorsteuerungen von Vorteil

- Kenntnisse in der Integration von Anlagen und Systemen

- Gute Kenntnisse von Stromnetzen, Netzformen und Netzverhalten

- Sicheres und kundenorientiertes Auftreten

- Lösungsorientierte und selbstständige Arbeitsweise, Qualitätsbewusstsein

- Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse, Englisch- und Französischkenntnisse von Vorteil

- Führerausweis Kategorie B

- Reisebereitschaft ca. 50 %

- Pikettdienst

Was Dich auszeichnet 

- Systemisches Denken – Du erkennst Zusammenhänge, auch an Anlagen, die Du nicht selbst gebaut hast

- Analytische Stärke – Du findest Ursachen, nicht nur Symptome

- Hands-on & pragmatisch – Du bist gerne dort, wo die Anlage steht

- Ruhe beim Kunden – Du behältst den Überblick, wenn etwas nicht läuft, und erklärst verständlich, was Du tust

- Umsetzungsstärke – Du bringst Dinge zu Ende

Bist Du das? 

Du bist nicht der Typ, der nur tauscht, was kaputt ist. Du verstehst, warum eine Anlage so aufgebaut ist – und sorgst dafür, dass sie auch nach Jahren im Betrieb zuverlässig läuft. Bei uns arbeitest Du an Anlagen, bei denen es zählt, dass sie wirklich laufen.

Was Dich bei uns erwartet

Technik, die zählt: 

Du arbeitest an Notstromsystemen, die im Ernstfall funktionieren müssen – kein Spielplatz, sondern echte Verantwortung.

Abwechslung: 

Einsätze beim Kunden und Engineering im Haus, etwa zur Hälfte.

Stabilität trifft Wachstum: 

Ein etabliertes Unternehmen mit klarer Richtung – und gleichzeitig genug Dynamik, um Dinge wirklich voranzubringen.

Interessiert? Dann freuen wir uns auf Deine Bewerbung!

title: Homologation & Certification Engineer, Energy Systems
description:
About EH Energy Engineering 

EH Energy is developing cutting-edge fuel cell technology for heavy-duty mobility and large-scale stationary power applications. Our uniquely redesigned product delivers a significantly more compact fuel cell system with high power density and lower production costs. In response to the challenges of climate change and the global shift toward decentralized energy, EH Energy provides high-performance, cost-effective fuel cell solutions to our clients and partners.

To support our rapid growth and bring our systems to global markets, we are seeking a Certification Engineer. In this critical role, you will take full ownership of our product compliance roadmap, bridging the gap between innovative engineering and strict global regulations. You will lead hazard and risk assessments, define certification strategies across international markets (EU, North America, marine), and interface directly with notified bodies and classification societies to ensure our fuel cell systems are safe, fully compliant, and market-ready.

This role requires a full-time, on-site presence at our office in Nyon, Switzerland . We are unable to offer remote or hybrid arrangements , so candidates should be based locally or prepared to relocate .

Key responsibilities 

Certification strategy and project management 

- Identify applicable directives, regulations, harmonised standards and class rules early in the development cycle and translate them into design requirements (EU, North America, marine)

- Select and manage notified bodies, NRTLs, classification societies and test laboratories, own budgets, schedules and contracts for certification work

- Plan and witness type tests, factory acceptance tests (FAT) and site acceptance tests (SAT)

Safety engineering and risk analysis 

- Lead risk assessments to ISO 12100 and hazard studies (HAZID, HAZOP to IEC 61882)

- Lead design and process FMEA (IEC 60812) for stacks, balance of plant, containers and fuel processing

- Run explosion-protection assessments: hazardous area classification (IEC 60079-10-1), ventilation and gas detection concepts, and equipment selection

- Specify and verify safety functions to ISO 13849 (PL) and IEC 61508, including safety requirement specifications and validation reports

Compliance and technical documentation 

- Compile and maintain technical construction files, CE Declarations of Conformity, type-approval dossiers and certification reports

- Write and review user, installation, operation and maintenance manuals, safety instructions and labelling

- Maintain the standards register and assess the impact of new or revised standards

- Manage certification change control: assess design changes for impact on existing certificates

Collaboration and continuous improvement 

- Act as the internal authority on certification scope: ensure in-service conformity of series production with certified designs, and support procurement and supply chain on material and packaging compliance (e.g. RoHS, packaging regulations).

- Support design reviews and supplier qualification, including component certificates (ATEX, PED, electrical)

Standards and regulatory scope 

The role covers, but is not limited to, the frameworks below. Working knowledge of most is expected; deep expertise in several is required

- IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1:2021, ISO 16110-1 and Machinery Regulation (EU) 2023/1230

Required qualifications 

- Master’s or bachelor’s degree in mechanical, electrical, chemical, process or safety engineering, or equivalent

- 5+ years in product certification, compliance or safety engineering for complex electromechanical or process equipment (energy, gas, process, machinery or marine)

- Direct experience with hydrogen or fuel cell systems and the IEC 62282 series, CSA/ANSI FC 1 or ISO 16110

- Proven track record of taking products through CE marking and third-party certification with notified bodies or NRTLs

- Hands-on experience leading FMEA, HAZOP and risk assessments, and documenting them to auditor standard

- Solid knowledge of ATEX / IECEx, hazardous area classification and explosion-protection concepts

- Experience specifying and validating safety functions to ISO 13849 and/or IEC 61508

- Excellent technical writing: clear, structured, audit-ready technical files and manuals

- Fluent English, written and spoken

Preferred qualifications and personal profile 

Nice to have 

- Marine type approval with a classification society (DNV, LR, BV, ABS) or IGF Code projects

- Experience with fuel processing, reformers or fire equipment, and with pressure equipment under PED

- Certified functional safety qualification or ATEX/IECEx competence certification

- Familiarity with North American codes (NEC, NFPA) and UL/CSA certification

Personal profile 

- Rigorous and structured, with a strong safety mindset and an eye for detail

- Pragmatic: finds compliant solutions that keep development moving

- Confident communicator with engineers, auditors, authorities and customers

- Self-driven in a fast-growing, scale-up environment; comfortable owning topics end to end

Start date: Immediately

What we’re looking for

- Approximately 65% of your time traveling across Europe for customer meetings, executive workshops, pilots, and industry events.

Reporting structure 

You’ll report directly to our VP of Global Revenue , for territory strategy, customer relationships, and international expansion and will participate in weekly pipeline reviews, forecasting, and sales process alignment with the US team.

- Brief Background Check and Reference Check

Compensation 

The estimated compensation range for this role is 280-340k CHF OTE , 50/50 split, depending on experience and skill set.

Our compensation follows a standard 50/50 enterprise sales structure consisting of base salary and target commission. High performers are eligible for uncapped commission accelerators above quota.

title: Clinical Solutions Consultant
description:
About Rivia 

Rivia is a technology company building a data engine that powers the future of clinical trial intelligence. Rivia was founded on the belief that new drugs can be brought to market more successfully with a fraction of today's capital.

Biotechs are the source of most therapeutic innovation, yet clinical development is constantly constrained by fragmented data and outdated tooling. Rivia unifies clinical trial data at scale through a core engine built as a reusable intelligence layer, comprising hundreds of configurations and trial-specific logic, independent of source structure. This vertical stack of data engine, workflows, and agents creates a distinct advantage in how trials are operated.

Over the past two years, European- and US-based biotechs running global clinical trials on Rivia have demonstrated measurable impact, from earlier understanding of therapeutic potential to significantly more efficient trial execution. In March 2026, Rivia raised its $15M Series A led by Earlybird Venture Capital.

Rivia's ambition is to become the standard infrastructure for modern drug development, transforming how trials are executed end-to-end.

The Role 

As our Clinical Solutions Consultant, you'll be the bridge between science, technology, and sales, helping biotech and pharma companies understand how Rivia can transform the way they work with clinical trial data.

You'll partner closely with our Account Executives throughout the technical stages of the sales cycle, turning complex scientific and technical challenges into compelling product demonstrations, tailored sandboxes, and solutions that address real customer needs.

This isn't a role where you simply present slides or follow a demo script. You'll need to understand clinical trial workflows, get hands-on with data, challenge assumptions, and translate complex customer requirements into solutions we can actually deliver.

You'll also play an important role in shaping how we approach technical pre-sales at Rivia, building repeatable processes, improving our demo environments, and helping us scale without losing the scientific depth and customer understanding that make us different.

What Excites You 

- Bringing science and technology together: You love understanding complex scientific challenges and translating them into practical, impactful solutions.

- Being hands-on: You don't just talk about what a product can do. You enjoy building demos, configuring sandboxes, working with data, and showing customers what's possible.

- Making an impact on revenue: You enjoy being part of the sales process, influencing strategic deals, and helping customers confidently make decisions.

- Solving real customer problems: You're curious about how biotech and pharma companies operate and enjoy finding creative ways to address their challenges.

- Building from the ground up: You get excited about joining a growing company where you can shape processes, improve tools, and help establish how technical pre-sales should work.

- Working across teams: You enjoy collaborating with Sales, Product, and Engineering, balancing commercial opportunities with technical feasibility.

Responsibilities 

- Partner with Account Executives as the scientific and technical expert throughout the sales process, helping prospects understand how Rivia can address their specific challenges.

- Lead in-depth product demonstrations tailored to customers' clinical trial workflows, data structures, and scientific requirements.

- Build and configure customized sandboxes, demo environments, and prototype integrations to demonstrate Rivia's value using realistic customer scenarios.

- Understand customers' clinical trial pipelines, protocols, endpoints, and data challenges, translating their needs into practical technical solutions.

- Scope prospective customer implementations, identifying technical requirements, dependencies, risks, and feasibility before commercial commitments are made.

- Collaborate closely with Solutions Engineers and Customer Engagement to ensure smooth handovers from pre-sales to implementation.

- Act as a trusted technical advisor to both customers and internal teams, confidently addressing complex scientific questions while being transparent about product capabilities and limitations.

- Adapt demonstrations and technical conversations to customers' familiarity with and readiness to adopt AI-driven solutions.

- Identify recurring customer needs, technical objections, and product gaps, sharing insights with Product and Engineering to continuously improve our offering.

- Help develop scalable pre-sales processes, reusable demo environments, and technical documentation as Rivia grows.

What Excites Us 

- Scientific background: You have a degree in life sciences, bioinformatics, biomedical engineering, or a related scientific discipline, and you're comfortable navigating complex scientific discussions.

- Relevant experience: You bring at least 4 years of client-facing experience in solutions consulting, technical pre-sales, field application science, technical account management, or similar roles.

- Scientific and technical fluency: You understand scientific data and experimental logic, and can quickly grasp complex clinical trial workflows and technical requirements.

- Hands-on technical skills: You've personally built and configured product demos, sandboxes, or technical proof-of-concepts, rather than only presenting solutions developed by others.

- Commercial mindset: You understand how technical expertise contributes to winning deals and enjoy working closely with sales teams to move opportunities forward.

- Customer-facing confidence: You can communicate complex technical concepts clearly and credibly, whether you're speaking with scientists, clinical operations leaders, or technical stakeholders.

- Strong ownership: You're proactive, independent, and comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where processes are still being built.

- Collaborative approach: You know when to challenge assumptions, push back on unrealistic commitments, and work across teams to deliver the best outcomes for customers.

Bonus / Nice to Have 

- Previous experience in scientific software, clinical trial technology, biotech platforms, or laboratory informatics.

- Familiarity with clinical trial protocols, endpoints, regulatory considerations, and clinical data integration.

- Experience working with AI-driven products or communicating the value of AI to scientific and technical stakeholders.

Our Values 

- In It to Win It: Approach every challenge with determination, resilience, and a drive to achieve the best possible outcomes.

- Embrace Change: We see change as an opportunity for growth, innovation, and improvement, continuously evolving to stay one step ahead.

- Why Not?: We challenge assumptions, stay curious, and explore new possibilities rather than accepting things as they are.

- Find the Gap: We proactively identify opportunities, anticipate challenges, and solve problems before they arise.

- Collective Accountability: We're one team, on one mission, committed to shared responsibility, mutual support, and trust.

- Value Add Solutions: Know better. Act better. We're dedicated to delivering meaningful solutions that create real impact.

description:
Du bist Student: in der Ernährung und Diätetik und möchtest deine Ausbildung mit der offiziellen Qualifikation als Ernährungsberater: in in der Schweiz abschliessen?

Für das dafür obligatorische, einjährige Zusatzmodul (Praktikumsjahr) suchen wir motivierte Nachwuchstalente: Wenn du praxisnah lernen möchtest, wie moderne ambulante Beratungen funktionieren, und wertvolle Erfahrungen an der Schnittstelle von persönlicher Patient*innenbetreuung und zukunftsweisender Digital Health sammeln willst, ist unser Graduate-Internship genau das Richtige für dich.

Für unser Oviva-Team in der Schweiz suchen wir dich per Oktober 2027 als Des. Ernährungsberater*in BSc .

Warum Oviva? 

Bei Oviva verfolgen wir eine klare Mission: Wir wollen eine nachhaltige, personalisierte und klinisch wirksame Versorgung für alle zugänglich machen.

Unsere digitalen Programme unterstützen Menschen mit gewichtsbedingten Erkrankungen. Für viele ist Gewichtsverlust ein Ziel, doch unser Ansatz geht weit darüber hinaus: Wir helfen, die Gesundheit zu verbessern, Selbstvertrauen aufzubauen und die Lebensqualität zu steigern.

Wir haben bereits über eine Million Menschen in der Schweiz, Deutschland, Polen und Grossbritannien unterstützt – und wir stehen erst am Anfang. Jedes Gespräch, jedes Coaching und jede Zeile Code bringt uns einer gesünderen Zukunft näher. Werde Teil unseres Teams und gestalte diese Zukunft aktiv mit.

Dein Verantwortungsbereich 

Als Graduate / des. Ernährungsberater*in machst du dich Schritt für Schritt mit dem Arbeitsalltag einer Fachperson im ambulanten Beratungssetting vertraut und baust deine Handlungskompetenz kontinuierlich auf:

- Ambulante Ernährungstherapie: Du führst Beratungen von Erwachsenen, Kindern und Jugendlichen durch – zunächst eng begleitet vor Ort in unseren Partnerpraxen und digital, später eigenständig mit Vor- und Nachbesprechungen (Praxisauslastung ca. 1–4 Beratungen pro Halbtag).

- Zuweisermanagement & Vernetzung: Du arbeitest interprofessionell mit Ärzt*innen sowie medizinischem Praxispersonal zusammen, stärkst Beziehungen und unterstützt bei der Gewinnung und Entwicklung regionaler Partnerpraxen.

- Wissensvermittlung: Du konzipierst und führst Fachwebinare (z. B. für MPA) durch und hältst praxisnahe Vorträge an Fachveranstaltungen sowie internen Weiterbildungen.

- Qualität & Projekte: Du erstellst und überarbeitest hochwertige Beratungshilfsmittel, nimmst regelmässig an internen Fallbesprechungen teil und unterstützt bei regionalen Marketingprojekten.

- Office-Präsenz: Jeden Mittwoch bist du vor Ort in unserem Büro in Zürich präsent, tauschst dich mit anderen Graduates aus und vertiefst dein Netzwerk.

Das bringst du mit 

- Ausbildung: Du stehst kurz vor dem Abschluss deines Bachelorstudiums (des. Ernährungsberater*in BSc) an einer Fachhochschule (z. B. BFH) in Ernährung und Diätetik.

- Arbeitsweise: Du arbeitest selbständig, flexibel und bist top organisiert.

- Begeisterung: Du hast Freude an der persönlichen sowie digitalen Patient*innenbegleitung und bist offen für unterschiedliche Fach- und Indikationsgebiete.

- Standort-Flexibilität: Du arbeitest flexibel im Homeoffice sowie digital, bist jedoch jeden Mittwoch verbindlich vor Ort in unserem Office in Zürich.

- Sprachen: Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift setzen wir voraus; gute Englischkenntnisse sowie weitere Sprachen sind ein grosses Plus.

Deine Benefits bei Oviva 

- Strukturierter Berufseinstieg: Ein massgeschneidertes Graduate-Programm mit gezielter Einarbeitung, Supervision und enger Begleitung auf dem Weg in die selbständige Beratung.

- Vergütung & Spesen (Basis 100 % Pensum): 

- Grundgehalt: CHF 2'525.– pro Monat

- Feste Spesenpauschalen: CHF 225.– Monatsspesen, CHF 30.– Telekommunikation sowie CHF 137.50 Reisespesen-Zusatz für Graduates

Unser Praktikum findet in der Regel mit einem Pensum von 80 % statt.

- Modernste Arbeitsmittel: Eine eigenentwickelte, innovative App und Beratungssoftware, die administrative Abläufe erleichtert.

- Teamkultur & Vernetzung: Ein dynamisches, interdisziplinäres Team, in dem Wissen geteilt und Erfolge gemeinsam gefeiert werden.

- Sinnstiftende Arbeit: Eine Unternehmenskultur, bei der Patient*innenzufriedenheit und Behandlungsqualität an erster Stelle stehen.

(a) = alle: Vielfalt ist uns wichtig.

Es ist uns sehr wichtig, eine Kultur zu haben, in der die Menschen gerne arbeiten wollen. Dies erreichen wir, indem wir unsere Werte bei allem, was wir tun, in den Vordergrund stellen:
Patient*innen stehen bei uns an erster Stelle, Wir befähigen unsere Teams, Wir machen es möglich.

Oviva engagiert sich leidenschaftlich dafür eine inklusive Kultur zu schaffen, die die unterschiedlichen Stimmen unserer Mitarbeiter*innen ermutigt, unterstützt und feiert. Wir sind ein wirklich inklusiver Arbeitsplatz, an dem man selbst sein kann und alle willkommen sind.
Wir begrüßen und ermutigen Bewerberinnen mit allen Hintergründen und Identitäten einschließlich, aber nicht beschränkt auf Nationalität, ethnische Zugehörigkeit, Geschlecht, sexuelle Orientierung, Alter, Fähigkeiten, Religion und sozioökonomischen Status. Wir suchen aktiv nach Kandidatinnen, die eine einzigartige Perspektive mitbringen, um uns beim Aufbau eines stärkeren, inklusiven Teams zu helfen.

Oviva engagiert sich für die Unterstützung von Kandidat*innen und Mitarbeiter*innen mit Behinderungen.

title: DevOps Engineer
description:
In a world where geopolitical tensions and security threats are accelerating, the way nations protect people and preserve peace is being redefined. For a long time, innovating in defense was about making tougher hardware. But with the evolution of software and the recent AI disruption, the future of defense is shifting to software-powered unmanned systems that save lives by removing humans from the front line. This is our mission.

At Intelic, we're building the intelligence layer for unmanned systems in defense. As a software-first company, we enable autonomous platforms to operate together - faster, smarter, and more reliably - across complex, mission-critical environments. Our technology turns disconnected assets into coordinated forces, helping operators make accurate decisions when it matters most.

Based in Amsterdam and growing fast, Intelic offers a rare opportunity to work on products that don't just move metrics - they meaningfully impact safety, resilience, and the future of Europe's security.

Why This Role Exists

Nexus has to run in places most software never goes: offline, in the field, installed and operated by people who are not developers. Getting it there in one piece, and keeping it running, is a job on its own.

Right now that job sits mostly with three backend engineers who cover this alongside their own work. As Nexus grows, so does the team, and we're adding someone to take real ownership of the pipelines, installers, and infrastructure that turn Nexus into something operators can trust, and who treats security as part of how the work gets done, not a separate project bolted on afterwards.

What You Will Do

You will join Product Adoption, the team that owns the last stretch between working software and a field-ready product: deployment, installers, monitoring, and everything that keeps Nexus running once it leaves the building. We are hiring at medior to senior level, roughly a 2 to 3, with room to flex higher for the right person.

- Build and maintain the CI/CD pipelines that turn Nexus into an installable, field-ready product across Linux and Windows

- Maintain and harden our software supply chain, including dependency scanning and package security

- Own the Windows installer and service orchestration, and help developers debug the platform-specific issues that come with it: permissions, firewalls, services, "works on my machine"

- Secure the software update server, the one online touchpoint in an otherwise offline system, and keep telemetry from the field reliable without leaking sensitive data

- Harden APIs and authentication on the surfaces that face the outside world

- Maintain and gradually take over our on-prem infrastructure: physical servers, backups, and disaster recovery, as we move away from renting machines in the cloud

- Build small internal tools, mostly in Python, Rust and shell or PowerShell scripts: installers, updaters, and the occasional internal or customer-facing web app

- Support incident response when things break in production, and help build the monitoring that catches problems before customers do

- Write down what you learn, so the next person, including future you, doesn't have to debug the same thing twice

You'll Thrive Here If

- You bring solid experience with CI/CD pipelines and build automation

- Comfort working across both Linux and Windows, with the ability to actually debug problems on either, not just deploy to them

- Experience with infrastructure as code (Ansible, OpenTofu, or similar)

- A security mindset: hardening, secure defaults, and attack surface are just part of how you build things, not an afterthought

- Enough scripting or programming ability to read and contribute to Python, Rust, or shell scripts. There is there is plenty of custom tooling to build.

- A level head under pressure. You can prioritise and stay steady when a few things break at once

Nice to have: 

- Experience with on-prem, bare-metal or virtulized infrastructure, not just cloud consoles

- Familiarity with Docker

- Exposure to dependency and package scanning tools such as Sonatype

- An interest in platform or infrastructure engineering as its own discipline. We expect this to split into a dedicated function over time

- Ability to build in-house tooling where needed and integrate vendor solutions where they fit

What Your First Year Will Look Like

- You've taken over meaningful parts of the CI/CD pipeline and installer work independently, without needing step-by-step instructions

- You've hardened at least one exposed surface end to end, the update server, an API, or similar

- You've helped move part of our infrastructure off rented machines and onto hardware we run ourselves

- Developers come to you when something breaks on Windows or Linux, because you've built a track record of finding the actual root cause

- You've documented enough of what you know that the team is less dependent on any one person, including you

Why Intelic

- We are setting up an environment, largely from the ground up that has to approved by MoDs

- You won't be bored. New projects, new problems, and a steady stream of things nobody has solved here before

- Real ownership from day one, not ticket-taking. If you see a better tool or approach, you're free to try it

- You'll work with hardware that matters: servers you can walk up to, deployments running in places with no internet, problems that cloud-only engineers rarely see

- A small team that leans on each other. When someone's on leave, the rest pick up the slack, and vice versa

- The mission is real. Nexus supports operators in the field, and how well you build and secure it has a direct effect on whether it works when it counts

What We Offer

- Stock Appreciation Rights programme (equity)

- A vibrant office at NDSM Plein, Amsterdam Noord — where we come together in person every day, because we believe it matters for the kind of work we do

- Flexible pension plan

- 25 vacation days

- Travel allowance

- Urban Sports corporate membership

- Lease a Bike option

Please note that, as part of our recruitment process, we may request a Certificate of Conduct (VOG) and conduct a background screening in accordance with our screening policy. We appreciate your understanding and cooperation throughout this process.

title: Senior Backend Engineer (Rust)
description:
About Intelic 

In a world where geopolitical tensions and security threats are accelerating, the way nations protect people and preserve peace is being redefined. At Intelic, we're building the intelligence layer for unmanned systems in defense: software that enables autonomous platforms to operate together, faster, smarter, and more reliably, across complex, mission-critical environments.

Based in Amsterdam and growing fast, we offer a rare opportunity to work on products that don't just move metrics. They directly affect safety, resilience, and Europe's security.

Why the role exists 

Our drones carry more and more hardware: cameras, gimbals, servos and more. The European market is fragmented, so we need to support many different types of hardware. Right now, adding a new piece of hardware usually means our own engineers have to integrate it. We want to change that. We're building a platform that lets partners and other teams connect their own hardware and write their own driver.

You'll work alongside robotics engineers and help set the team up from the start. The APIs and system design you create will be what everyone else builds on.

If you like hard backend problems where good design directly affects how fast other people can move, this role is worth a look.

What you will do 

You'll spend most of your time in Rust, working out how to abstract the communication with the hardware from the rest of the system. That could mean designing how a new camera gets configured through the API, or writing a simulated camera so you can test an integration before the hardware is on your desk.

- Design and build the platform in Rust

- Define the APIs that other teams and partners use to integrate cameras, gimbals, servos and other hardware

- Make it possible for others to write their own drivers and add hardware without needing support from your team

- Think through how each new module fits into the wider system, and plan for the cases others will run into later

- Write strong unit tests and add integration tests, including tests against simulated hardware

- Work directly with other teams to understand what they need from the platform and agree on how systems talk to each other

- Help set up the team, and hand it over well once the platform is in good shape

You will thrive here if 

- You have around five or more years of engineering experience in a heavy backend language. Rust is ideal, C++ or similar also works

- You've built platforms or APIs that other teams depend on, and you think about how your part fits into the larger system

- You work independently. You take a problem, work it out with the team, and see it through without someone managing every step

- You talk to people. You reach out to other teams, ask questions, and don't wait for work to come to you

- You take testing seriously, and you know how to test code that talks to hardware

- You use AI coding tools like Claude in your day to day work

- You enjoy technical problems more than product decisions. Here, what needs to be built is fairly clear. The job is to build it well

Bonus if you have: 

- Basic hardware knowledge: you know how to power a camera and get video out of it

- Experience with drones, robotics or other connected hardware

How we work 

We're a startup, so we plan about three months ahead and things can change after that. The team you join is small and may not stay in its current form forever. Once the platform is set up, you may move on to work on the wider vehicle platform.

- Strong unit testing is the standard. Integration tests are added where they make sense, often using simulated hardware

- Other teams build on your APIs and integrate their own hardware, so you don't have to do every integration yourself

- Engineers work directly with other teams to agree on interfaces

What your first year will look like 

At 6 months: You own this part of the system. The platform is set up, and the team is working at the level you helped set.

At 12 months: The platform runs without you in the middle of it, and you're helping on the wider vehicle platform, including the flight side.

Why Intelic 

- The mission is real. We're building technology that makes Europe safer.

- Your work multiplies. Set the platform up well, and every team can integrate new hardware without waiting on anyone.

- You build it from the start. You shape the APIs and the team instead of maintaining someone else's design.

- You can focus on engineering. The problem is clear. Your job is to solve it well.

What we offer 

- Stock Appreciation Rights program

- Travel allowance

- Flexible pension plan

- 25 vacation days

- Urban Sports Club membership

- Bike lease through 'Lease a Bike'

- A modern office at NDSM Plein, Amsterdam Noord. We value working shoulder to shoulder, so we're in the office 4 days a week. You also get 10 days a year to work from wherever you want.

title: Backend Engineer
description:
Engineering · Amsterdam (hybrid) 

Inner Circle is a dating app for people who are done wasting time. Every member is screened thoroughly, so the profiles you see are people worth dating. 

Every AI-powered feature starts with the data and infrastructure behind it. From building scalable backend systems to powering smarter matching and personalisation, our engineers turn data into meaningful connections - and shape how AI transforms the future of dating. 

Goal of the Role 

You power the engine that brings more members together every second. We’re moving our backend from a PHP monolith to Kotlin services, and changing how we build software at the same time: AI and agentic engineering are part of how our team works every day. You’ll join the team building the new part of our system, and occasionally work in our legacy PHP codebase. 

You don’t need prior PHP or Kotlin experience. We care more about how you think and approach problems than about which language you have used so far. 

Tech stack: Kotlin, Spring Boot, GraphQL, PHP 8 (legacy), MySQL (Aurora), Redis, OpenSearch, RabbitMQ, Docker, Kubernetes (EKS), AWS (S3, SNS/SQS, SES, Rekognition, and more), DataDog 

Result Areas: 

Build and ship features that matter to members 

Deliver backend features that improve matchmaking, engagement and retention. You work from outcome-based stories: the team agrees on the result, and you own how to get there. 

Help move our platform to Kotlin services 

Build new Kotlin services and help extract functionality from the PHP monolith step by step, without disrupting the members who use the app every day. 

Work with AI, and with judgement 

Use AI and agentic tools such as Claude Code in your daily work. Give them clear specs and context, and review what they produce as critically as you would review a colleague’s code. 

Own the quality of what you build 

Write clean, testable code with automated tests, keep pull requests small, follow secure coding practices, and stay responsible for your code once it runs in production. 

Make pragmatic trade-offs 

Reason through problems and ship solutions that are good enough. Recognise when something needs more care or optimisation, and ask for input when a decision is bigger than your part of the system. 

What you bring: 

- 3+ years of experience in backend engineering 

- Proficiency in at least one typed backend language, such as Kotlin, Java, C#, Go, TypeScript or PHP 

- Solid experience with APIs and relational databases, including query performance 

- Understanding of systems design and software architecture, and the ability to reason about trade-offs 

- You know why clean code matters and you apply it, with or without AI 

- Experience writing automated tests and working with CI/CD 

- Hands-on experience with AI coding tools, or a strong drive to learn agentic engineering practices 

- Clear communication in English, both spoken and written (design docs, decision records, pull request descriptions) 

Nice to have: 

- Experience with AWS 

- Experience with event-driven systems or microservice architectures

In 2019, we built the first mobile-first insurance platform, enabling insurance to be accessible online by millions in the region. Today, it’s the leading insurance platform in Southeast Asia.

The Role 

Doit is building its investment business from Vilnius. As Head of Compliance and AML at Doit Lithuania, you will build and run our compliance and anti-money-laundering function from day one.

You will act as our Compliance Officer and AML Officer, and report directly to the management board. You will be independent of the business lines you monitor. You will run compliance and AML for a digital investment platform serving clients in Lithuania and across the European Economic Area.

What You’ll Own 

- Write and own the compliance and AML/CTF policies and procedures.

- Build the business-wide AML risk assessment, customer risk scoring and risk appetite.

- Design remote onboarding controls with our KYC partners, including enhanced due diligence for PEPs and high-risk clients.

- Design and tune transaction monitoring scenarios for brokerage activity.

- Run sanctions screening at onboarding, on an ongoing basis and on payments.

- File suspicious activity reports with the FNTT and suspicious order reports under MAR.

- Run the compliance monitoring programme and report to the board.

- Approve marketing communications and oversee product governance, complaints and conflicts of interest.

- Manage the regulatory relationship with the Bank of Lithuania on compliance and AML matters.

- Prepare the firm for the EU AML Regulation, which applies from July 2027.

- Build the compliance and AML team as the business grows.

What We’re Looking For 

- Significant experience in AML/CTF at a regulated EU financial institution. Ideally at an investment firm, neobroker, neobank or e-money institution.

- Experience with digital onboarding and remote identity verification at scale.

- Hands-on experience building risk assessments, monitoring scenarios and EDD processes.

- Experience filing suspicious activity reports and handling regulatory inspections.

- Knowledge of MiFID II conduct and investment-services compliance, or the ability to learn it fast.

- Experience selecting and overseeing KYC, screening and monitoring tools.

- Strong judgment and the confidence to challenge senior colleagues.

- Clear, concise writing for policies, board reports and regulators.

- A clean record and good reputation, suitable for regulatory approval as a key function holder.

- Based in Lithuania, or open to relocating to Lithuania.

Nice to Have 

- Lithuanian language ability.

- An existing working relationship with the Bank of Lithuania or the FNTT.

- Knowledge of Lithuanian AML law and Bank of Lithuania instructions.

- Experience with clients across several EEA countries.

- CAMS (ACAMS) or ICA certification.

This Role Is Not For 

- People who only want to attend meetings.

- Candidates who cannot follow up aggressively and professionally.

- People who copy policies from templates without fitting them to the business.

- People who say no without offering a compliant way forward.

- People who produce long updates without clear decisions or next actions.

Location 

This role is based in Vilnius, Lithuania. This is a hybrid role. You are expected to work from our Vilnius office at least 3 days per week.

You must be a European citizen or already hold a valid right to work in Lithuania. We are not able to offer visa sponsorship for this role.

Language 

English is our main working language across global teams. Strong English communication is required.

- Role-specific interview

title: Account Executive, Strategic Deals - Attribute™, EMEA
description:
Account Executive, Strategic Deals - Attribute™ 

Location 
This is a fully remote opportunity based out of any of the following with travel as needed: UK, Ireland, Netherlands, Sweden, Estonia.

Who We Are 
Become part of the team behind Attribute™ . Following our recent acquisition, we're bringing together visionary engineers and go-to-market leaders to disrupt cloud management with real-time, tagless cost visibility across cloud and AI workloads. As an Account Executive focused on Strategic Deals, you'll join a founding GTM movement inside an established market leader trusted by over 4,500 global customers, unlocking high-impact opportunities through top-tier strategic partnerships.

DoiT empowers cloud-native organizations to scale faster and innovate with confidence. By combining our Cloud Intelligence technology with Forward Deployed Engineers and deep specialization across AWS, Google Cloud, and Azure, we help tech-forward companies navigate their toughest infrastructure and cost governance challenges end to end.

The Opportunity 
As an Account Executive, Strategic Deals for Attribute™ , you will be at the forefront of building a brand-new region from scratch and introducing a groundbreaking solution to a fundamental business problem in modern FinOps. You will work on Strategic Deals, leveraging strategic partnerships with AWS, OpenAI, Top Private Equity firms, and our global current install base. A strong focus will be placed on co-selling and unlocking strategic deal opportunities with AWS, ISVs, and channel partners. Traditional cloud cost allocation methods rely heavily on static tagging—an approach that becomes obsolete in modern, shared cloud and AI infrastructure. When multi-tenant clusters, shared GPUs, microservices, and dynamic AI workloads dominate, organizations face severe blind spots: they cannot accurately determine the true cost-to-serve for specific applications, autonomous agents, or business teams, making it impossible to calculate true gross margins at a granular customer level.

Attribute™ solves this by taking a completely different approach. Leveraging runtime eBPF technology, Attribute™ captures real-time network traffic signals and kernel-level observability without requiring engineering teams to manually tag or instrument code. By analyzing actual runtime consumption across CPU, GPU, memory, network, and AI model API requests, it provides accurate total cost of ownership (TCO) and unit economics based on real usage. Organizations finally get precise cost governance and gross margin visibility across complex cloud and AI environments with zero developer overhead.

As an Account Executive building this region from scratch, you will establish a high-potential greenfield territory. You will drive sales end-to-end with a heavy emphasis on net-new logo acquisition, defining the regional go-to-market strategy and creating the foundational customer success stories that define this category.

You will own full-cycle deal execution across Startup, Digital Native, and Enterprise segments—prospecting new accounts, running compelling solution pitches, navigating complex technical evaluations alongside engineering partners, and closing strategic partnerships end to end.

You'll have the rest of the Cloud Intelligence portfolio behind you: 4,500 customers, AWS/Google Cloud/Azure partnerships, and Forward Deployed Engineers who solve problems other vendors walk away from. But the product you'll carry every day is Attribute™, and the market is only just learning it exists. That's the opportunity.

Expect to travel 10–15% of the time to meet customers, engage with hyperscale teams, and show up at industry events that matter.

Responsibilities 

- Own the full sales cycle from first conversation to closed deal, consistently hitting and exceeding quota and pipeline targets

- Build a high-volume pipeline and establish the region from scratch with a hunter mindset, driving outbound prospecting and net-new logo acquisition across EMEA

- Build the first wave of reference customers and case studies the rest of the GTM org will run on

- Develop and execute a regional strategy that identifies high-growth opportunities and untapped markets across EMEA

- Build deep, mutually valuable relationships with AWS Sales Leaders and Partner Managers to co-sell and expand market share

- Partner with Forward Deployed Engineers and Solutions Architects to solve the toughest technical challenges prospects face

- Maintain rigorous forecast accuracy in Salesforce and ensure every proposal reflects the quality of what we actually deliver

As AI becomes the primary interface to the web, this layer will replace the role of traditional search engines.

We are designing these systems to search and reason over web data in real time, under strict latency and reliability constraints. This means solving retrieval, ranking and passage extraction under entirely new access patterns and at significant scale, with systems operating over constantly changing, unstructured data and serving tens of thousands of production workloads 24/7.

Bringing the latest advances from the research community to our search stack and ship it to production.

Your responsibilities:

Mentor researchers and engineers and help raise the technical bar of the team

- 
Proven track record of shipping ML or AI systems to production at scale

- 
Deep experience with search, retrieval, ranking or building RAG-based assistants

Strong understanding of modern deep learning, especially transformers and embeddings

- 
Experience with LLM-integrated or knowledge-intensive systems

- 
Experience designing evaluation frameworks and metrics for ML systems

- 
Strong programming skills in Python

- 
Top-tier publications ( ICLR , ICML , NeurIPS, AAAI , EMNLP , ACL )

Nice to haves

title: Model Risk Officer
description:
Build with us

Since 2004, we've had one clear goal: to make payments and money management effortless for every business in Europe.

Today, more than 250,000 companies use Mollie to get paid, manage money and grow, with products designed to be simple, scalable, and dependable.

With 950+ Mollies across 14+ locations, we care deeply about autonomy and craft. So we work in small teams, with real ownership, and we trust you to make the right decisions.

We're building for the long term, so we provide the tools you need, processes you can rely on, and a balanced work environment to help you do work you're proud of.

Sound like your kind of place? Let's build together.

Your impact

Credit, IRRBB and capital models sit at the heart of how a bank measures its own risk. Mollie already uses models in day to day processes, but nobody challenges them independently from a second line perspective yet. As Model Risk Officer, you'll help build the second line model risk function that gives Mollie, and its regulator, confidence that models can be trusted before they're used.

This is a true 0 to 1 role. Mollie isn't a bank today, so there's no model risk framework, validation methodology or model inventory to inherit. You'll design the policy, validation approach and governance from scratch, starting with the credit, IRRBB and capital models already in design for our future capital and liquidity planning. Your work feeds into our licence application and, once authorised, into how we manage model risk every day.

You'll also work with our Machine Learning team and the Domains already deploying models, so you can shape how we manage model risk today, not just in a banking future. Your challenge and sign off will be visible to senior leadership, audit and, eventually, our regulator. As Mollie grows and matures its model risk management, your scope grows from building the framework to running an ongoing model risk cycle.

What you'll ship

- Build and own Mollie's model risk management framework and policy, including model risk appetite, validation standards and the model risk lifecycle.

- Set up and maintain the model inventory for credit, IRRBB and capital models, with materiality and risk tiering for each.

- Coordinate independent second line validation and challenge before models are used, including credit risk and ECL, IRRBB, and Pillar 1 and Pillar 2 capital models.

- Design the ongoing monitoring and re-validation cycle with the Machine Learning team, covering performance testing, limitation tracking and re-validation triggers.

- Partner with model owners in Credit Risk and Treasury ALM, and coordinate within the second line Risk function, so model risk challenge is built into the wider risk and capital frameworks.

- Coordinate clear, well documented validation reports and model risk information that stand up to scrutiny from DNB/ECB, external auditors and internal audit.

What you'll bring

- Around 5 to 7 years of experience in model risk management or model validation within a bank, preferably across at least one of credit, IRRBB and capital models.

- Solid working knowledge of ECB model risk expectations and how model validation should be structured and evidenced.

- Comfort building a model risk framework and validation approach from the ground up. You're excited to write the first playbook.

- Strong quantitative skills to critically assess model methodology, assumptions and performance, and the discipline to document your findings so others, including a regulator, can follow them.

- The ability to explain model limitations and validation findings to model owners and senior stakeholders, and the confidence to hold your ground under challenge.

- Genuine curiosity about how AI can speed up the parts of model validation that don't need a human, so more of your time goes toward judgement and challenge.

Grow your way

At Mollie, growth is personal. We believe everyone should have the chance to develop their skills, explore new challenges and shape their career on their own terms.

You'll get regular feedback and performance reviews to support your development, with fair and transparent salary reviews along the way. Many Mollies move into new roles or take on new projects to stretch themselves, and we actively hire from within to help you take the next step.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

Unlock your full potential and join us to eliminate financial bureaucracy

If you're excited by the idea of building what's next, for yourself and for thousands of businesses across Europe, we'd love to hear from you. Apply with your CV (in English) using the form below.

Want a peek behind the scenes? Check out what life at Mollie is really like.

AI at Mollie

We believe in Always Be Shipping, and AI brings that philosophy to life across every team, every role, every day.

AI is core to how we build. It helps us move faster, simplify work and make smarter decisions, creating real impact for the businesses we serve. We're looking for people who are excited to use AI to shape the future of finance with us.

Success in this role requires a unique blend of skills and traits 

- 7+ years of experience (the more the better) in an offensive security role.

title: Customer Service Agent
description:
Bij Crisp staan onze klanten op nummer één. Ons gezellige en hechte serviceteam doet er alles aan om die klanten van de beste service te voorzien. We hebben daarom veel persoonlijk contact met de klant, en ondersteunen onze bezorgers voor een vlekkeloze bezorging. We zijn nog volop in ontwikkeling, dus je denkt ook mee over hoe we onze service kunnen verbeteren.

Wat je gaat doen

Je hebt elke dag direct contact met onze klanten, vooral via Whatsapp. Zo maak je ze nog blijer nadat ze ons gesproken hebben. Daarnaast geef je feedback van klanten door aan de juiste teams binnen Crisp, zodat we onze service kunnen blijven verbeteren. Ook zorg je samen met onze bezorgers en je collega's op onze logistieke hubs dat bezorgingen vlekkeloos verlopen. Verder verdiep je je in onze processen. Zoals je al hoort, geen dag is hetzelfde!

Hoe ziet een werkdag eruit? 

- 's Ochtends hou je onze bezorgroutes goed in de gaten. Is het druk op de weg? Dan zorg jij ervoor dat onze klanten op tijd weten dat hun bezorger iets later is.

- Ondertussen pak je WhatsApp-berichtjes van klanten op. Je helpt ze met het aanpassen van hun bestelling, het kiezen van een bezorgtijd of beantwoordt vragen over ons assortiment. Zo leer je elke dag iets nieuws over eten!

- Lunchtijd! Elke dag lunchen we met onze eigen boodschappen. Een ideaal moment om ons assortiment én je collega's beter te leren kennen.

- Na de lunch beantwoord je vragen via WhatsApp, social media en e-mail, terwijl je collega's de bezorgingen in de gaten houden of bezig zijn met de processen. Je merkt dat er veel vragen zijn over een bepaalde marketingactie. Dat geef je dus meteen even door aan de juiste collega.

- De collega's die 's avonds werken nemen jouw taken over. Dat zorgt ervoor dat je de feedback die klanten doorgeven via de app nog even kunt verwerken.

- Tijd om af te sluiten. Samen met je collega's drink je nog een ijskoud Crisp-drankje in onze gezellige keuken.

Dit ben jij

Je herkent je in het volgende profiel:

- Je bent parttime (16-24 uur per week) beschikbaar. We zijn 7 dagen per week open van 07:30 tot 23:00 uur, en je werkt straks in shifts van 4 tot 8 uur. Daarom is flexibele beschikbaarheid voor overdag, avonden én in het weekend een must.

- Je woont in omgeving Amsterdam en bent voor minimaal één jaar beschikbaar.

- Een kantoor in de Amsterdamse Pijp met een grote keuken waar flink wordt geluncht, gezellig gekookt en waar de kans op zelfgebakken taart of vegan roze koeken groot is. Goed om te weten: vanaf januari 2027 groeien we door en verhuizen we naar een gloednieuwe, grotere locatie in de buurt van Zaandam, Sloterdijk en de Houthavens, waar we vanaf dan onze nieuwe thuisbasis hebben. 

- Je schrijft en spreekt vloeiend Nederlands. Op een persoonlijke en creatieve manier reageren op klanten gaat jou makkelijk af.

- Je bent oplossingsgericht en empathisch. Je kunt je verplaatsen in onze klanten en begrijpt wat er nodig is om hun ervaring met Crisp nog beter te maken.

- Je bedenkt creatieve oplossingen om onze klanten te verrassen en verwachtingen te overtreffen.

- Als je klantenservice-ervaring hebt binnen organisaties waar kwaliteit hoog in het vaandel staat, is dat super!

Wat wij bieden

- Een marktconform salaris, afhankelijk van leeftijd.

- Een gezellig en hecht team.

- Veel verantwoordelijkheid, uitdagend werk en een dynamische omgeving.

- Een kijkje in de keuken van een snelgroeiende start-up. We zijn volop in ontwikkeling dus jouw ideeën tellen mee.

- Werken bij een B-Corp gecertificeerd bedrijf, waarbij je de kans krijgt om je stempel te drukken op ons voedselsysteem en échte verandering teweeg te brengen

- Enthousiaste en ondernemende collega’s om mee te werken en te leren.

- Voor straks een perfect pensioen via BPFL.

- Voor nu een persoonlijk budget voor yoga, sport, mobiliteit en downtime via bijvoorbeeld ClassPass, Pathé en Blendle.

- Elke maand food for thought, met workshops en talks via de Crisp University.

- Tijd om je collega’s te leren kennen tijdens sport, events en proeverijen.

- Een kantoor in de Amsterdamse Pijp met een grote keuken waar flink wordt geluncht, gezellig gekookt en grote kans op zelfgebakken taart of vegan roze koeken.

- En... fikse korting op je Crisp boodschappen, omdat je thuis natuurlijk ook goed wilt eten.

Ben jij geïnteresseerd?

Is de functie van Service Agent jou op het lijf geschreven, solliciteer dan via onderstaand button. Hoe meer je kunt delen over jezelf en de reden dat je solliciteert, hoe beter.

Bij Crisp streven we naar een inclusieve en diverse werkomgeving waarin iedereen welkom is, ongeacht hun achtergrond, geslacht, leeftijd, etniciteit, seksuele geaardheid, religie of beperking. Wij moedigen sollicitanten met diverse perspectieven en achtergronden aan om te solliciteren en geloven in gelijke kansen voor iedereen. We waarderen de unieke bijdragen die elke medewerker kan leveren en zijn vastbesloten om een inclusieve werkplek te creëren waarin iedereen wordt gerespecteerd en gewaardeerd.

description:

As SkyNRG grows, applications such as SAP Public Cloud, HubSpot, and our Inventory Management System are becoming increasingly important to our operations.
